question: What is the process to upgrade an unmanaged package that is currently installed in production?
optionA: Install the new version to a Developer org then deploy to production.
optionB: Uninstall the current version and install the new version.
optionC: Click the update link on the Installed Packages page.
optionD: Use the Install Wizard to install the upgrade to production.
explanation:
Uninstalling the current version and installing the new version is the process. Unmanaged packages cannot be upgraded — Salesforce Help says so directly ("Unmanaged packages aren't upgradeable") — so once installed, the only way to get a newer version of an unmanaged package into an org is to uninstall the existing one and install the new one.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (install to a Developer org, then deploy to production) — deploying the package's components would collide with the version already installed; it does not upgrade it.
Option C (the update link on Installed Packages) — the update link is a managed-package feature; it does not appear for unmanaged packages.
Option D (the Install Wizard to install the upgrade) — the installer refuses a second install of an unmanaged package with the same namespace of components already present; the existing version has to come out first.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.pkg1_dev.meta/pkg1_dev/packaging_developing_unmanaged.htm

question: An app builder would like to streamline the user experience by reflecting summarized calculations of specific fields on various objects. Which field types could be used in roll-up summary fields to accomplish this? Choose 3 answers.
optionA: Currency
optionC: Date
explanation:
Currency, Percent and Date are the field types a roll-up summary can summarise. Roll-up summary fields aggregate values from child records in a master-detail relationship, and the field being summarised must be numeric or date-based: Currency, Number and Percent support SUM, MIN and MAX, and Date fields support MIN and MAX. (COUNT works on any related record regardless of field type, but the question is about which field types can be summarised.)
Why the other options are wrong:
Option D (Checkbox) — not a numeric or date field; it cannot be the aggregated field.
Option E (Time) — not supported as a roll-up summary source either.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_roll_up_summary_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks (CK) increased its Salesforce development efforts so that it now has multiple custom development efforts happening in parallel. CK's developers and admins perform the customizations and have complained that working in one sandbox has led to many problems. They requested a solution in which they can work in at least 20 different sandboxes at once, that all start with the same base configuration and data. What should an app builder use to solve the problem?
optionA: Sandbox refreshes
optionC: Partial copy sandboxes
explanation:
Sandbox cloning is the feature written for this scenario, and Salesforce describes it in almost the stem's words: 'You can create a sandbox by cloning an existing sandbox rather than using your production org as your source. Save time by customizing a sandbox with a set of data and metadata and then replicating it. Sandbox cloning simplifies having multiple concurrent streams of work in your application life cycle... Your colleagues can easily clone individual sandboxes instead of sharing one sandbox and avoid stepping on each other's toes.' That covers all three requirements — parallel streams of work, escaping a single shared sandbox, and every environment starting from one common baseline, since 'when you clone a sandbox, its data and metadata are copied to the new sandbox.'
The sandbox types cannot deliver the same thing, because each one copies from production rather than from a prepared baseline. Developer sandboxes are the type that ships in quantity, and they carry metadata only, which is precisely why cloning is what gets a common set of data into them. One practical note the documentation adds: 'A cloned sandbox uses the same license type as its source org', so cloning organises the environments rather than conjuring extra licences.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (sandbox refreshes) — a refresh only re-copies an existing sandbox from its source; it creates no new environments.
Option B (Full copy sandboxes) — the least plausible at this count: one or two per org, and each a complete copy of production rather than of the team's baseline.
Option C (Partial copy sandboxes) — 'includes a copy of your production org's configuration (metadata) and a sample of your production org's data as defined by a sandbox template', so twenty of them would each be a fresh slice of production, not twenty copies of the agreed starting configuration; and Partial Copy is a paid add-on rather than something available in twenties.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.data_sandbox_cloning_overview.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.create_test_instance.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Answer moved C->D. The Sandbox Cloning article matches this stem clause by clause — 'multiple concurrent streams of work', colleagues cloning 'instead of sharing one sandbox', and 'customizing a sandbox with a set of data and metadata and then replicating it' for the common baseline. The old key rested on Partial Copy being licensed in larger quantities than Full, which is true but does not reach twenty, and misses the real defect: every sandbox type copies from production, so no quantity of fresh Partial Copies gives twenty environments sharing one prepared configuration. Cloning is also what puts data into Developer sandboxes, which are the type that actually ships in quantity and otherwise carry metadata only.

question: Cloud Kicks (CK) wants to set up a custom child object to track gift cards issued to a customer. A key requirement is to track the total number of gift cards opened and gift cards issued on an Account. CK wants to permanently ensure the gift cards are unable to be moved across any other Account once it is created. On the gift card object, what type of field should be created to support this requirement?
optionA: Master-detail relationship
optionC: Formula
explanation:
A master-detail relationship is the field type to create on the gift card object. With 'Allow reparenting' unchecked (the default), a master-detail relationship prevents child records from being moved to another parent — satisfying the 'unable to be moved across any other Account' requirement — and it enables roll-up summary fields on the Account to count gift cards opened and issued.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (roll-up summary) — lives on the parent, not the child, and it needs the master-detail relationship to exist first.
Option C (formula) — cannot relate the gift card to an Account or lock it there.
Option D (lookup relationship) — allows the parent to be changed and does not support roll-up summaries.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_roll_up_summary_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.overview_of_custom_object_relationships.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: At Universal Containers, all US Sales Reps should be able to view the US Team dashboard. However, only the US Sales Directors should be able to see the data in the component and view its source report. How can an app builder ensure the proper access is granted?
optionA: Make the US Sales Director the running user and share the dashboard folder with the role US Sales Rep.
optionB: Make the dashboard dynamic and give US Sales Reps the View My Team's Dashboard permission.
optionC: Share the dashboard folder with roles and subordinates of the US Sales Director and share the report folder with the role of US Sales Director.
optionD: Share the dashboard with the public group US Sales Reps and share the dashboard source reports folder with the US Sales Director profile.
explanation:
Sharing the dashboard folder with roles and subordinates of the US Sales Director, and the report folder with the US Sales Director role, is how the access is granted. Folder access is what separates the two audiences: sharing the dashboard folder with Roles and Subordinates of the director gives every rep beneath that role the ability to open the dashboard, while sharing the source report's folder only with the director role means only directors can open the underlying report — the drill-down half of the requirement.
One mechanism worth being precise about, because it is easy to state backwards. Restricting the report folder does not hide the numbers rendered in the dashboard. A dashboard runs as its running user, and Salesforce's own worked example of Viewer access describes a sales rep who checks his standing on a dashboard and 'must view the data in the underlying reports' yet needs nothing more than 'Viewer access to the folder that contains the Master Sales dashboard'. So reps who can open this dashboard will see the component values; what they will not be able to do is open or drill into the source report. Read the requirement's 'see the data in the component' as being about reaching the report behind it rather than about the summary figures on the dashboard face.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (director as running user, folder shared with the rep role) — changes whose data is shown without restricting report access.
Option B (dynamic dashboard with View My Team's Dashboards) — a dynamic dashboard shows each viewer their own data and cannot be the answer to a shared team dashboard.
Option D (share the dashboard with a public group, the report folder with a profile) — dashboards are not shared directly; access is granted through folders.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.analytics_folder_viewer.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.analytics_folder_access.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Key C stands, but the old explanation was wrong on mechanism and has been corrected. It claimed that 'by restricting the report folder, only directors can see the underlying numbers'. The Viewer Access article contradicts that with a worked example: a sales rep who refreshes a dashboard and views the data in its underlying reports needs only Viewer access to the dashboard's folder. Dashboard components render as the running user, so report-folder access controls drill-down, not whether the component displays values. That makes the stem's 'see the data in the component' imprecise — flagged rather than silently confirmed, since a learner could otherwise take away a false model of dashboard security. The key is still the best answer because it is the only option that grants reps the dashboard while confining source-report access to directors.

question: Cloud Kicks is redefining its entire business process to convert the Manager Notes field from a long text area field. The goal is to encourage managers to be more concise in their comments and stay at 255 characters or less. There is preexisting information in the Manager Notes field that often is well beyond the character limit. What would happen to any existing information if the app builder tries to convert a preexisting long text area field to text area?
optionA: Preexisting information will truncate to the first 255 characters.
optionB: Preexisting information will remain even if it was over 255 characters.
optionC: Preexisting information will cause an error message to pop up.
optionD: Preexisting information in the field will be completely lost.
explanation:
Preexisting information will truncate to the first 255 characters. When converting a Long Text Area to Text (max 255), Salesforce truncates existing values to the first 255 characters; the setup screen warns that data may be truncated, but the conversion proceeds and the excess characters are lost.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (information remains even over 255) — a Text field cannot hold more than 255 characters, so the overflow cannot survive.
Option C (an error message pops up) — the conversion warns and proceeds; it does not refuse.
Option D (completely lost) — the first 255 characters are kept; only the remainder is dropped.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.notes_on_changing_custom_field_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which Opportunity standard fields are available to be configured directly? Choose 3 answers.
optionA: Forecast Category
optionC: Lead Source
explanation:
Stage, Lead Source and Type are the Opportunity standard fields that can be configured directly. All three are standard picklist fields whose values can be edited directly in Object Manager.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Forecast Category) — derived automatically from the Stage value, configured through the Stage picklist's Forecast Category mapping rather than directly.
Option E (Probability) — also tied to Stage; each Stage value carries its default probability.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.faq_forecasts_category_mapping.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A new field has been added to the Applicant object that is part of an unmanaged package. A recruiter ran the Position with or without Applicants report and noticed that the new field was missing as an option to add as a column. How should an app builder troubleshoot this issue?
optionA: Adjust the field-level security to include in the report type.
optionB: Check Allow Reports for the Position and Applicant objects.
optionC: Add the field to the custom report type field layout.
optionD: Update the profile with the Manage Public Reports permission.
explanation:
Adding the field to the custom report type's field layout is how the app builder fixes it. Custom report types do not automatically include new fields added to an object; the app builder must edit the custom report type and explicitly add the new field to its field layout to make it available as a column in reports built from that report type.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (adjust field-level security) — FLS controls whether a user may see the field, but a field absent from the report type's layout is unavailable regardless of FLS.
Option B (check Allow Reports on the objects) — Allow Reports makes an object reportable at all; both objects already are, since the report runs.
Option D (Manage Public Reports permission) — governs saving reports to public folders; nothing to do with which columns a report type offers.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000384387&language=en_US&type=1
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.reports_manage_report_type.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An app builder received a request to extend record access beyond the organization-wide defaults configured. Which two features satisfy this requirement? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Sharing Rules
optionC: Permission Set Groups
explanation:
Sharing rules and manual sharing are the two features that extend record access beyond the org-wide defaults. Sharing rules grant access to groups of users based on ownership or criteria; manual sharing grants access to specific users or groups on individual records.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (public groups) — containers used inside sharing rules and manual shares; they grant no access on their own.
Option C (permission set groups) — bundle object, field and system permissions, not record-level access.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.managing_the_sharing_model.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers manages leads in a Lead qualification queue where sales reps can accept ownership of the Lead. Campaign members are required to have a sales owner. What validation rule should an app builder configure?
optionA: AND( ISBLANK(Lead.Owner.Id) )
optionC: AND(ISNEW(), ISBLANK(Owner:User.Id))
explanation:
NOT(ISBLANK(Owner:Queue.Id)) is the validation rule. Campaign members must have a sales (user) owner, so the rule should fire whenever the Lead is owned by a queue — that expression returns TRUE when the owner is a queue, blocking the save and forcing a sales rep to take ownership.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (AND(ISBLANK(Lead.Owner.Id))) — every lead has an owner, so this never fires; and Lead.Owner.Id is not how a validation rule on Lead references its own owner.
Option B (NOT(ISNEW() && ISBLANK(Owner:Queue.Id))) — fires on every edit of a user-owned lead and never on a queue-owned one; the logic is inverted.
Option C (AND(ISNEW(), ISBLANK(Owner:User.Id))) — only blocks new records, not existing ones being edited while still owned by the queue.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_creating_cross_object_notes.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An app builder wants to create a report to compare the number of support cases in each status (New, In-Progress, or Closed) and by priority (Critical, High, Medium, or Low). What solution should be used for the report?
optionA: Grouping
optionC: Custom Report Type
explanation:
Grouping is the solution. Grouping rows by Status and columns by Priority — a matrix report, or a summary report with two groupings — produces exactly the comparison the requirement describes.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (bucket columns) — categorise values into custom groups; the Status and Priority values are already the categories wanted.
Option C (custom report type) — defines which objects and fields are reportable; it does not compare counts.
Option D (filters) — narrow the data shown; they do not break counts out by two dimensions.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.reports_builder_fields_groupings.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Sales reps want the ability to see who can view their account records and how the people have access. Which button should the app builder add to the Account page layout to enable this?
optionA: New Task
optionC: Sharing Hierarchy
explanation:
Sharing Hierarchy is the action that shows who can see a record and why. Who Has Access to Account Records? gives the two routes: "To find out why a user has access to the record, in Lightning Experience, click Sharing Hierarchy from the Action Menu on the account record. Click View next to the user's name. In Salesforce Classic, click Sharing on the account detail page, then click Expand List to see all users who have access. Click Why? next to the user's name." The Spring '21 release note adds that "Sharing Hierarchy is now available on the action menu, not just in the Share window", and it is added to the layout's Salesforce Mobile and Lightning Experience Actions like any other action. Note that the same page says the Sharing Hierarchy and Sharing buttons appear only when the org-wide default is not Controlled by Parent or Public Read.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (New Task) — creates an activity; nothing to do with access.
Option B (Sharing) — in Lightning Experience the Sharing action opens the Share window for granting manual shares; the who-has-access-and-why view is reached through Sharing Hierarchy. Sharing is the right button only in Salesforce Classic, where its Sharing Detail page lists users and a Why? link.
Option D (Edit) — edits the record's fields.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.granting_access_to_records_lex.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.faq_record_access.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=release-notes.rn_forcecom_sharing_view_record_access_lex.htm&language=en_US&release=232&type=5

corrected.note: In Lightning Experience the record access view is the Sharing Hierarchy action: "click Sharing Hierarchy from the Action Menu on the account record. Click View next to the user's name" to see each user's access and the reason for it (Who Has Access to Account Records?). The Sharing button is the Salesforce Classic route (Sharing, then Expand List, then Why?). The old explanation also claimed Sharing Hierarchy shows role-hierarchy access only and cannot be added to the layout; both claims are contradicted by the documentation. The 2026-09-05 exam dump keys Sharing Hierarchy.

question: An app builder is tasked with adding key performance indicators on Account pages. They want to see a summary of the number of open Opportunities and the number of won Opportunities for each Account. Where should the app builder go to build these new rollups?
optionA: Lightning App Builder
optionC: Lightning Object Creator
explanation:
The Account object is where the app builder builds these rollups. Roll-up summary fields are created on the parent (master) object, and Account is the master in the Account–Opportunity relationship, so the roll-up summary fields counting open and won Opportunities are created on Account.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Lightning App Builder) — places components on pages; it creates no fields.
Option C (Lightning Object Creator) — creates a new custom object from a spreadsheet; not where fields are added to Account.
Option D (Opportunity object) — the child side; a roll-up summary lives on the parent it summarises into.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_roll_up_summary_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: When an Opportunity Close Date is pushed more than 30 days, manager approval is required. An approval process is in place but reps frequently forget to submit for approval to run the process. How can an app builder ensure that these opportunities are submitted into the approval process?
optionA: Change the entry criteria on the approval process to criteria are met and lock the record on initial submission.
optionB: Use a validation rule and an email alert to the manager requesting approval.
optionC: Submit the record for approval from an automated process.
optionD: Give the manager the API Enabled permission to permit approval responses by email.
explanation:
Submitting the record for approval from an automated process is how the app builder ensures the opportunities enter the approval process. A record-triggered flow (or Process Builder) can call the Submit for Approval action automatically when the Close Date is pushed by more than 30 days, removing the need for the rep to remember.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (entry criteria plus locking on submission) — entry criteria decide whether a submitted record is accepted; they never submit it. Submission is always an explicit action.
Option B (a validation rule and an email alert) — a validation rule blocks the save rather than submitting anything, and an email is not an approval request.
Option D (API Enabled for the manager, approval by email) — approval responses by email are a separate setting and concern how the manager responds, not whether the rep submits.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_ref_elements_actions_approval.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers wants to deliver purchased containers to remote construction addresses. In these cases, the customers will supply UC with the coordinates to the location. What type of field should the app builder use to capture this information?
optionA: Number
optionC: Text
explanation:
A Geolocation field is the type to use. It stores latitude and longitude as a compound field and supports distance calculations in formulas, reports and SOQL — the native field type for capturing coordinates.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Number) — would need two separate fields and gives no distance functions.
Option C (Text) — stores the coordinates as a string with no validation and no distance calculation.
Option D (External Lookup) — relates a record to an external object; nothing to do with coordinates.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.custom_field_types.htm&type=5&language=en_US

question: DreamHouse Realty (DR) asks for some improvements in case management. They want to enforce process compliance so that cases are unable to be reverted to an earlier case status, and to ensure that certain fields are required when specific case criteria are met. Which solution should an app builder implement to meet these requirements?
optionA: Configure validation rules with help text.
optionB: Create dependent picklist fields and set them as required.
optionC: Use an approval process to check field criteria are met.
optionD: Make the fields required on the page layout.
explanation:
Configuring validation rules with help text is the solution. Validation rules can compare PRIORVALUE(Status) to the new Status to block backward moves, and can conditionally require fields based on other field values — something page-layout Required cannot do, since that makes the field required unconditionally. Both compliance requirements are met with validation rules.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (dependent picklists set as required) — a dependent picklist constrains values by a controlling field; it cannot stop a status going backwards or require unrelated fields conditionally.
Option C (an approval process checking criteria) — approvals gate a submitted record; they do not enforce field rules on every save.
Option D (required on the page layout) — unconditional, and bypassed by the API; it cannot express "required when specific criteria are met".
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_field_validation.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.customize_functions_priorvalue.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: To increase adoption, Universal Containers is proposing changes to its Salesforce data model to allow easier visibility for sales reps into key metrics. The proposal has three custom objects related to the Account object, one with a master-detail, and two that are not. Each of these objects has 15 fields they would like to summarize on the Account object. What are two considerations for this proposal? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Roll-up summaries allow MAX, MIN, SUM, COUNT, and AVG.
optionB: An object can have 20 object references.
optionC: An object can have 25 roll-up summaries.
optionD: Roll-up summaries are limited to master-detail relationships.
explanation:
An object can have 25 roll-up summaries, and roll-up summaries are limited to master-detail relationships — those are the two considerations. Roll-up summary fields can only be created across master-detail relationships, so the two lookup-related objects cannot be summarised natively; and the standard limit is 25 roll-up summary fields per object (raisable to 40 by Salesforce), which 15 fields from even the one master-detail object approaches.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (MAX, MIN, SUM, COUNT and AVG) — roll-up summaries support COUNT, SUM, MIN and MAX, not AVG.
Option B (20 object references) — the relationship-field limit is not what constrains this proposal; three related objects are well within it.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_roll_up_summary_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) has created a picklist field called Status on three separate custom objects. UC has a requirement to share the list of values for this field across each object. Which feature would an app builder use?
optionA: Field Update
optionC: Dynamic Action
explanation:
A Global Picklist Value Set is the feature. A global value set is a single, centrally managed list of picklist values that can be reused by picklist fields on multiple objects, ensuring consistency and one-place maintenance.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Field Update) — a workflow action that writes a value; it does not define a value list.
Option C (Dynamic Action) — controls which actions appear on a page; nothing to do with picklist values.
Option D (Dependent Picklist) — constrains one picklist's values by another's on the same object; it does not share a value list across objects.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_creating_global_picklists.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: On the Account Lightning record page, users need to see ten fields and the ability to sort and wrap text on their Related Lists. What Related List type would the app builder select for the Related List Lightning component?
optionA: Enhanced List
optionC: Related List — Single
explanation:
Enhanced List is the related list type to select. The Related Lists — Enhanced component supports up to 10 columns, inline text wrapping and column sorting, which is exactly the ten fields plus sort and wrap the users need.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Basic List) — displays only a few fields and lacks sort and wrap.
Option C (Related List — Single) — the component for one related list; the type question is still enhanced versus basic, and on its own it does not deliver the ten sortable columns.
Option D (Related List List View) — not a related list type in the component's picker.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.customizing_related_lists.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Ursa Major Solar's service department gets requests for several types of services, such as installation, repair, and maintenance. Service managers need to be able to tell when maintenance was last done on an asset to help determine if they are meeting contract agreements, but the last maintenance date can be difficult to determine when there are many work orders related to the asset. They think it would be helpful to have a field auto-populated on the Asset record when a maintenance work order gets closed. What tool should an app builder recommend to help meet this requirement?
optionA: Visualforce
optionC: Apex Trigger
explanation:
Flow is the tool to recommend. A record-triggered flow on Work Order can detect when the status changes to Closed and the type is Maintenance, then update the related Asset's Last Maintenance Date field — declaratively.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Visualforce) — a page technology; it does not react to a work order closing.
Option B (Roll-up Summary) — Asset to Work Order is a lookup, not master-detail, so no roll-up summary can be built.
Option C (Apex Trigger) — would work, but it is code where a flow does the job declaratively.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_build_data_update.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_roll_up_summary_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Northern Trail Outfitters has two custom objects that are part of a master-detail relationship. What determines the ownership and sharing access of the detail record?
optionA: The default owner is set in the parent object's settings.
optionB: The Owner field on the Detail record.
optionC: The Owner field on the Master record.
optionD: The owner is set independently on the detail object's settings.
explanation:
The Owner field on the Master record determines the ownership and sharing of the detail record. In a master-detail relationship the detail record has no Owner field of its own; ownership and sharing are inherited from the master record's owner.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (a default owner in the parent object's settings) — no such setting exists; ownership comes from each master record.
Option B (the Owner field on the Detail record) — detail records in a master-detail relationship do not have an Owner field.
Option D (set independently on the detail object's settings) — the detail cannot own itself; that is the point of master-detail.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.overview_of_custom_object_relationships.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The Director of Marketing at Northern Trail Outfitters wants the app builder to create a formula field that tracks how many days have elapsed since a contact was sent a marketing communication. The director is only interested in whole units. Which function should be used to return a date for calculating the difference?
optionA: DATETIMEVALUE()
optionC: DATEVALUE()
explanation:
TODAY() is the function to use. It returns the current date as a Date value, and subtracting one Date from another yields a whole number of days, which is what the director wants.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (DATETIMEVALUE()) — converts a value to Date/Time, which introduces the fractional part the director does not want.
Option C (DATEVALUE()) — converts a Date/Time or text to a Date, but the formula needs the current date, which DATEVALUE() does not supply on its own.
Option D (NOW()) — returns Date/Time and would produce fractional results.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.formula_using_date_datetime.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers is expecting impacts to operations due to increased demand. The executive team will be reaching out to current customers and want to see the number of open cases for the account and parent account. Which tool could an app builder use to display the number of open cases on the Account page?
optionA: Flow
optionC: Approval Process
explanation:
Flow is the tool that can display the number of open cases on the Account page. Account to Case is a standard lookup relationship, not master-detail, so a native roll-up summary field cannot count cases — a common misconception. A record-triggered flow (or scheduled flow) that counts related open Cases and writes the total to a number field on the Account is the no-code answer.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Workflow) — cannot aggregate child records, and is past end of support.
Option C (Approval Process) — routes a record for approval; it counts nothing.
Option D (Roll-up Summary) — requires master-detail, and Account–Case is a lookup.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_roll_up_summary_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) wants to delete data in several fields for 5,000 lead records. UC exports the selected record IDs and fields that need to have data deleted in a CSV file. Which two steps should an app builder suggest to meet these requirements? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Select the correct record type.
optionB: Use Import Wizard to update Leads using the CSV file.
optionC: Select Insert Null Values in settings.
optionD: Use Data Loader to update Leads using the CSV file.
explanation:
Selecting Insert Null Values in the settings, and using Data Loader to update the Leads from the CSV, are the two steps. Data Loader's Insert Null Values setting, when enabled, lets blank cells in the CSV overwrite existing field values with null — clearing the data.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (select the correct record type) — record type has no bearing on clearing field values.
Option B (Import Wizard) — the Data Import Wizard ignores blank values, so it cannot be used to clear fields.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.faq_import_general_update_blank_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks (CK) tracks the support level of its customers on the Account record page. CK wants to show a text notification on a Case record page when the related Account is a platinum-level customer. How could an app builder meet this requirement?
optionA: Add a Rich Text component to the Case Lightning page and set the component visibility to show when the Account Support Level is Platinum.
optionB: Create a text-only Visualforce page, drag the Visualforce component into the Case page layout, and set its visibility to show when the Account Support Level is Platinum.
optionC: Create a text-only Visualforce page, clone the Case page layout, drag the Visualforce component into the page, and assign the layout to platinum cases.
optionD: Clone the Case Lightning page, add a Rich Text area to the new page, and assign this page to platinum accounts.
explanation:
Adding a Rich Text component to the Case Lightning page with its visibility set to show when the Account's Support Level is Platinum is how the app builder meets the requirement. In Lightning App Builder a Rich Text component supports component visibility filters that can reference fields on the related parent (Account.Support_Level__c) — the simplest declarative solution, with no cloning and no Visualforce.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (a Visualforce page with visibility on the page layout) — page layouts do not carry component visibility filters; that is a Lightning page feature, and the Visualforce page is unnecessary.
Option C (a cloned page layout assigned to platinum cases) — page layouts are assigned by profile and record type, not by a field value on the related account.
Option D (a cloned Lightning page assigned to platinum accounts) — Lightning pages are assigned by app, record type and profile, not by a field value, and this is a Case page, not an Account page.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.lightning_page_components_visibility.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.lightning_page_components_visibility_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks (CK) keeps track of its shoe inventory in Salesforce. When an order's status is changed to Activated, the inventory for the ordered shoe is reduced. At that point, a SOAP web service on the CK website must be called so that the website is updated to display the correct inventory amount for the shoe. What should an app builder use to communicate to the CK web service when a shoe's inventory has changed?
optionA: After-Save Record-Triggered Flow
optionC: Process Builder
explanation:
An After-Save Record-Triggered Flow is what should call the CK web service. The requirement is to reach an external SOAP endpoint when inventory changes, and the choice comes down to which automation can act after the record is saved and is still supported. An after-save flow can invoke an action — including an outbound message, or Apex that calls the service — once the inventory change is committed.
Be careful with the reason for rejecting the older tools, because it is about support rather than capability. Outbound messaging genuinely does call a SOAP endpoint: Salesforce documents an outbound message as one that 'sends a message to a designated endpoint', and outbound message actions are available to flows, workflow rules, approval processes and entitlement processes alike. So a workflow rule could technically have done this; what disqualifies it is that Workflow Rules and Process Builder reached end of support on 31 December 2025. Since outbound messaging is available to flows, the after-save flow is also how you would use it today.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Before-Save Record-Triggered Flow) — before-save flows can only set field values on the record that triggered them and cannot perform actions, so they cannot call anything outward.
Option C (Process Builder) — reached end of support on 31 December 2025; existing processes run, but it is not the tool to build this with now.
Option D (Workflow Rule) — capable of an outbound message, but past end of support for the same reason.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_build_data_update.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.approvals_automated_actions.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Key A stands, but the explanation's dismissal of outbound messaging was wrong and has been corrected. It claimed workflow outbound messages are 'SOAP-style notifications from Salesforce, not arbitrary web service calls', implying they could not satisfy the requirement. Salesforce documents an outbound message as sending 'a message to a designated endpoint' — that is a SOAP web service call, and it is the classic declarative way to make one. So options C and D fail on support status, not on capability: both Process Builder and Workflow Rules hit end of support on 31 Dec 2025. Rewritten so the reader takes away the correct model of outbound messaging, and so the before-save exclusion rests on its documented limitation of updating only the triggering record's fields.

question: Northern Trail Outfitters wants to change a master-detail relationship on Account to a lookup relationship with a custom object Park. The app builder tries to reconfigure this but is unable to do so. What could be causing this?
optionA: The Account is included in a flow process on the Park object.
optionB: The Park object needs at least one master-detail field for reporting.
optionC: The Account record includes Parks roll-up summary fields.
optionD: The Park records have existing formulas on the Account.
explanation:
The Account record including Parks roll-up summary fields is what blocks the change. Converting a master-detail to a lookup requires removing all roll-up summary fields on the master object that summarise the detail object first, since lookups do not support roll-up summaries; once the dependent roll-ups are deleted, the conversion can proceed.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Account included in a flow on Park) — a flow referencing the relationship does not prevent changing its type.
Option B (Park needs a master-detail field for reporting) — reporting does not require master-detail; lookups are reportable.
Option D (formulas on Account referencing Park) — a formula on the master cannot reference detail records; and cross-object formulas on the detail survive a change to lookup.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_roll_up_summary_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.overview_of_custom_object_relationships.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks has created a custom object called Interests which is joined to Accounts by way of a junction object called Account Interest. What is the impact to users attempting to view an Account and the associated Account Interest records if they are without read access to the Interest object?
optionA: Users will be able to view the Account Interest records and will have read-only access to the Interest records.
optionB: Users will be unable to view Account records that have a related Account Interest record.
optionC: Users will be unable to view the Account Interest records or the Interest records.
optionD: Users will be able to view the Account Interest record, but unable to view the field or any information relating back to the Interest record.
explanation:
Users will be unable to view the Account Interest records or the Interest records. On a junction object with two master-detail relationships, a user must have at least Read access to both parent objects to see any junction record; without Read on Interest, the user cannot see any Account Interest record, nor any Interest record.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (view Account Interest, read-only Interest) — no access to Interest means no access, not read-only access.
Option B (unable to view Accounts with a related Account Interest) — the Account record itself remains visible; only the junction and its other parent are hidden.
Option D (view Account Interest but not its Interest fields) — the junction record is hidden entirely, not shown with fields blanked.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.overview_of_custom_object_relationships.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.relationships_manytomany.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An app builder created multiple custom fields, page layouts, and reports in the sandbox and added them to a change set that was deployed to production. The reports were NOT deployed. What should the app builder do?
optionA: Move the reports to the Unfiled Public Reports folder and add them to a new change set.
optionB: Move the reports out of the Unfiled Public Reports folder into a public folder and add them to a new change set.
optionC: Recreate the reports in production. Reports are not supported in change sets.
optionD: Add the reports to an unmanaged package and install the unmanaged package into production.
explanation:
Moving the reports out of Unfiled Public Reports into a public folder and adding them to a new change set is what the app builder should do. Reports stored in personal folders or in the Unfiled Public Reports folder cannot be added to change sets; they must be moved into a shared public report folder before they can be packaged and deployed.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (move them to Unfiled Public Reports) — that is the folder they cannot be deployed from.
Option C (recreate them; reports are not supported) — reports are supported in change sets, just not from unfiled or personal folders.
Option D (an unmanaged package) — would work, but it is the wrong tool when the fix is a folder move away.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.changesets_about_components.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) wants to test code against a subset of production data that is under 5 GB. Additionally, UC wants to refresh this sandbox every weekend. Which type of sandbox should be used to accomplish this?
optionA: Developer Pro
optionC: Full Copy
explanation:
A Partial Copy sandbox is the type to use. Partial Copy sandboxes hold up to 5 GB of data based on a sandbox template and can be refreshed every 5 days, which allows a weekly refresh.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Developer Pro) — metadata only; it does not include production data automatically.
Option C (Full Copy) — refreshes every 29 days, so it cannot be refreshed weekly.
Option D (Developer) — metadata only, and a 200 MB data cap.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.data_sandbox_environments.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.create_test_instance.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers has a custom object that holds over 100 fields. The app builder wants to break up the fields into separate tabs on the Lightning page. Which Lightning component is most appropriate to fulfill this requirement?
optionA: Highlights Panel
optionC: Field Section
explanation:
Tabs is the most appropriate component. The Tabs component on a Lightning record page lets the app builder organise content into separate, named tabs — the natural way to split 100-plus fields into manageable groupings. The Accordion component is also valid for vertical collapsible sections, but the requirement specifically says separate tabs.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Highlights Panel) — shows a handful of key fields at the top of the page; it does not hold sections.
Option B (Record Detail) — renders the whole page layout in one block; the opposite of breaking the fields up.
Option C (Field Section) — groups fields within a Dynamic Form, but does not create separate tabs.
Option E (Accordion) — valid for collapsible vertical sections, but the requirement asks for tabs.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.lightning_page_components.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks wants to know the total value of all won Opportunities for Accounts and display it on the record. What type of summary should the app builder use in the roll-up summary field?
optionA: COUNT
optionC: SUM
explanation:
SUM is the summary type. SUM aggregates the numeric values of a field across child records; to get the total Amount of all won Opportunities for an Account, use SUM on Opportunity Amount with a filter for Won equals true.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (COUNT) — counts the records; it does not total their amounts.
Option B (MAX) — returns the largest single amount.
Option D (MIN) — returns the smallest single amount.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_roll_up_summary_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks has five years of sales data and would like to track when customers made their first purchase. How should an app builder use a roll-up summary to meet the requirements?
optionA: Create a new roll-up summary field called First Order Date, using type MIN on the Opportunity Close Date with a filter where IsWon = TRUE.
optionB: Create a new date field called First Order Date, create a workflow to set the date, and roll up the value with a filter where IsWon = TRUE.
optionC: Create a new roll-up summary field called First Order Date, using type SUM on Opportunity Close Date.
optionD: Create a new date field called First Order Date, then create a roll-up summary to update the field using type MIN.
explanation:
A roll-up summary field called First Order Date, using type MIN on the Opportunity Close Date with a filter where IsWon = TRUE, is how the app builder meets it. MIN of Close Date filtered to won opportunities returns the earliest won-opportunity date, which is the first purchase date, computed directly by the roll-up with nothing else to build.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (a date field, a workflow to set it, then roll up) — a workflow is unnecessary; the roll-up computes the value itself, and workflow is past end of support.
Option C (SUM on Close Date) — SUM cannot be applied to a date field.
Option D (a date field updated by a MIN roll-up) — a roll-up summary is its own field type; it does not update a separate date field.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_roll_up_summary_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The CFO of Cloud Kicks needs to sign off on any major shoe retail deal that has a discount of more than 30% before the deal can be closed. What feature would be used to handle this requirement?
optionA: Approval Process
optionC: Field Update
explanation:
An Approval Process is the feature. It formalises who must sign off, the criteria that trigger it, and what happens on approval or rejection — a CFO signing off on any deal discounted more than 30% before it can close is a textbook approval process.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Email Alert) — an individual action that notifies; it records no sign-off and blocks nothing.
Option C (Field Update) — an individual action that writes a value; no sign-off mechanism.
Option D (Workflow Rule) — could send the CFO an email, but cannot capture an approve or reject decision, and is past end of support.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.approvals_automated_actions.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.what_are_approvals.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks works on an annual subscription model. When a sales rep marks an opportunity as Closed Won, a new opportunity should automatically be created for the renewal. The contracts team works outside of Salesforce but also needs to be notified about closed deals in order to initiate the contract process with the customer. Which automation solution would meet these requirements?
optionA: Approval Process
optionC: Validation Rule
explanation:
A Record-Triggered Flow is the automation that meets both requirements. A flow on Opportunity that starts when the stage becomes Closed Won can create the renewal Opportunity record and send an email alert (or call an external service) to notify the contracts team — both requirements, declaratively, in one place.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Approval Process) — routes a record for sign-off; it neither creates a renewal record nor is triggered by closing a deal.
Option B (Outbound Message) — can notify an external system, but cannot create the renewal opportunity.
Option C (Validation Rule) — blocks a save; it creates nothing and notifies no one.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_build_data_update.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_ref_elements_actions_approval.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks wants to set up a new opportunity approval process and execute various action items based on the initial submission. Which three action types should an app builder use in the approval process? Choose 3 answers.
optionA: Email Alert
optionC: Task
explanation:
Email Alert, Task and Field Update are the three action types. Approval processes support exactly four action types: Email Alert, Task, Field Update and Outbound Message, and three of those are on the list.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (create a new record) — not an approval-process action; creating records is a flow capability.
Option E (invocable Process Builder) — not an approval-process action type, and Process Builder is past end of support.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.approvals_automated_actions.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An app builder has a custom component they want to make available on the utility bar, but the component is unavailable. How should the component be tagged?
optionA: For use on record pages.
optionB: For use in Lightning App Builder.
optionC: For use on the utility bar.
explanation:
The component should be tagged for use on the utility bar. A custom Lightning component must declare lightning__UtilityBar as a target in its .js-meta.xml configuration to be available as a utility item; without that target, App Manager does not expose it.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (for use on record pages) — the lightning__RecordPage target makes it available on record pages, not in the utility bar.
Option B (for use in Lightning App Builder) — the App Builder targets (app, home, record page) do not include the utility bar.
Option D (for use in App Manager) — App Manager is where the utility bar is configured, but there is no App Manager target; the utility bar has its own.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/targets-lightning-utility-bar.html
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/use-config-for-utility-bar.html

question: UC has a requirement that an Opportunity should have a field showing the value of its associated Account's Billing State. This value should not change after the Opportunity has been created. What is the recommended solution to configure this automated behavior?
optionA: Formula field
optionC: Workflow rule with Field Update (on create only)
explanation:
A workflow rule with a Field Update, evaluated on create only, is the recommended solution. The requirement is a value copied once at creation and then frozen, which rules out anything that recalculates. Automation that writes the value into a plain field on create and never runs again satisfies it: a workflow rule with a field update, configured to evaluate only when a record is created, copies Account Billing State into a text field on the Opportunity and leaves it alone thereafter.
One important currency note. Workflow Rules reached end of support on 31 December 2025. Existing rules continue to run and can still be edited, so the answer is not wrong, but a solution built today would use a record-triggered flow set to run only on record creation — the same design in the current tool.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (formula field) — wrong on principle rather than on detail: it evaluates every time the record is read, so if the Account's Billing State later changes, the Opportunity's displayed value changes with it — exactly what the requirement forbids.
Option B (Apex trigger) — would also work and is likewise frozen-on-create, but it is code where clicks suffice.
Option D (roll-up summary field) — doubly inapplicable: it aggregates child records across a master-detail relationship rather than copying a parent's field.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_roll_up_summary_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_build_data_update.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Key C stands, but the item needs a currency flag the old explanation only half gave. Workflow Rules reached end of support on 31 Dec 2025; per the established fact that this is retirement of support rather than removal of capability, an answer keying a workflow rule is still correct, but the explanation now says so explicitly and names the record-triggered flow equivalent instead of mentioning it in passing. Also strengthened the rejection of D, which the old text ignored: a roll-up summary aggregates detail records across a master-detail relationship and cannot copy a parent field at all.

question: Universal Containers is setting up Salesforce for the first time. Management wants the sales and marketing teams to have different navigation menus in the Salesforce mobile app. Which option is available to an app builder to satisfy the requirement?
optionA: Create sales and marketing profiles to ensure read access to different objects.
optionB: Create roles for sales and marketing and assign a custom homepage layout for each role.
optionC: Create separate Lightning apps with different navigation items for sales and marketing and assign each app to the corresponding profiles.
optionD: Create public groups for sales and marketing and create mobile navigation menus for each group.
explanation:
Creating separate Lightning apps with different navigation items and assigning each to the corresponding profiles is the option. In Lightning Experience and the unified Salesforce mobile app, mobile navigation comes from Lightning apps, so two apps with different navigation items, assigned by profile, give sales and marketing different menus. (The legacy Salesforce1 navigation menu was replaced by Lightning-app-based navigation.)
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (profiles with different object access) — object access changes what a user can open, not which navigation items they see.
Option B (roles with a custom homepage layout) — roles do not carry navigation, and home page layouts are not mobile menus.
Option D (public groups with mobile navigation menus) — navigation menus are not assigned to public groups; they belong to Lightning apps assigned by profile.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.salesforce_app_customize_lex_app.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.customize_lex_nav_menus_create.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An app builder needs to deploy a new Account detail page layout from sandbox to production. Which three components should an app builder include in the change set to ensure it deploys successfully and visually as expected? Choose 3 answers.
optionA: Detail page layout
optionC: Custom actions
explanation:
The detail page layout, the custom fields it references, and the custom actions placed on it are the three components to include. All three must travel together so the layout deploys successfully and looks the same in production: a layout that references a field or action absent from the target org fails to deploy.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option D (Lightning App Builder) — a tool, not a deployable component.
Option E (System Administrator profile) — profiles are not required to deploy a layout itself; the layout assignment can be made after deployment.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.changesets_about_components.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The sales team receives a list of approximately 800 leads each morning from the marketing team. The marketing team does not know if any of the leads are currently in the pipeline and sends the entire list each morning. Which tool should be used to import these leads into Salesforce while preventing duplicates from being inserted?
optionA: Dataloader.io
optionC: Data Loader
explanation:
The Data Import Wizard is the tool. It supports Lead imports natively and includes built-in duplicate matching — by name and email, among other options — so the morning list can be loaded without inserting leads already in the pipeline.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Dataloader.io) — a load tool without the wizard's built-in duplicate matching.
Option C (Data Loader) — no built-in dedupe logic; it would insert the whole list.
Option D (manual entry) — 800 leads a day by hand is not a process.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.for_leads.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An app builder wants to show Groups as the last navigation menu item in the mobile app. However, the app builder is unable to select Groups as one of the items on the drop-down menu. What could cause this?
optionA: Groups is available in the Recent section of the navigation menu.
optionB: Groups is included in the Smart Search Items but unavailable on the navigation menu.
optionC: Groups is unavailable in the selected list for the navigation menu.
optionD: Groups is available in the Chatter section of the navigation menu.
explanation:
Groups being available in the Chatter section of the navigation menu is the exam's answer, and the item is worth reading with care because the documentation does not describe the navigation menu the way the options assume. In the Mobile Only navigation menu, Groups is itself one of the available items, listed alongside Chatter rather than nested inside it: 'Groups — Appears for organizations that have Chatter enabled. If you don't add this item to the navigation menu, groups and the Groups item are automatically included in the set of Smart Search Items.' So two documented facts bear on the symptom: Groups is available only when Chatter is enabled for the org, and when it is not placed on the menu explicitly it still reaches users through Smart Search Items — which is also why placing it last in the menu is hard to achieve. The practical checks are whether Chatter is enabled for the org, and whether Groups is already accounted for in the Selected list or via Smart Search Items.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Groups in the Recent section) — the Recent section is built from the user's recently used items, not from the picker's configuration; it does not remove an item from the picker.
Option B (Groups in Smart Search Items but unavailable on the menu) — the documented fallback behaviour when Groups is not placed on the menu, and the closest real explanation; the exam keys the Chatter-section reading instead.
Option C (Groups unavailable in the Selected list) — restates the symptom rather than explaining it.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.salesforce_app_customize_nav_menu.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Key D left in place but this item looks defective and needs your decision — flagged rather than silently confirmed. The old explanation asserted that Groups 'appears in the Chatter section of the mobile navigation menu rather than as a standalone selectable item'. The Mobile Only Navigation Menu documentation contradicts both halves: it lists Groups as its own available item, and it describes no 'Chatter section' at all — Chatter and Groups are separate entries in the same list. What the documentation does describe is that Groups is available only when Chatter is enabled, and that if you do not add it to the menu, 'groups and the Groups item are automatically included in the set of Smart Search Items' — which is closer to option B than to option D. I did not move the key because option B as worded ('unavailable on the navigation menu') is not documented either, and I could not confirm the exact cause of an item missing from the picker. Recommended repair: reword the options around the documented facts, Chatter-enabled availability and Smart Search Items fallback.

question: The app builder needs to change the data types of new custom fields. The app builder is not able to delete and recreate any of the fields, nor modify any Apex code. Which data type change will require the app builder to perform additional steps in order to retain existing functionality?
optionA: Changing the data type of a field used in an Apex class from Number to Text.
optionB: Changing the data type of a field used in a report from Text to Encrypted.
optionC: Changing the data type of a field used as an external ID from Number to Text.
optionD: Changing the data type of a field used in lead conversion from Number to Text.
explanation:
Changing the data type of a field used in an Apex class from Number to Text is the change that requires additional steps, but not for the reason people usually give. Salesforce does not let the change through and then break the Apex: it refuses up front. "You can't change the data type of a custom field referenced by other items in Setup such as Visualforce pages, Apex code, processes, or flows." So the additional step is getting the reference out of the Apex first — and the stem forbids exactly that.
One thing worth carrying away beyond this question: a field type change is never free even when it is permitted. The conversion runs in the background over every existing record and "in some cases... can take over 24 hours to complete."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Text to Encrypted on a report field) — cannot be done at all, so it is not a matter of extra steps: "an existing custom field can't be converted into an encrypted field nor can an encrypted field be converted into another data type."
Option C (Number to Text on an external ID) — safe: an external ID only loses that behaviour when the new type falls outside text, number and email, and Number to Text stays inside that set.
Option D (Number to Text on a lead-conversion field) — blocked outright: "You can't change the data type of any custom field that is mapped for lead conversion."
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.notes_on_changing_custom_field_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Key A stands; the explanation had the mechanism backwards, which the spot-check of the first fifty questions caught. It said a Number to Text change "will cause compile errors in any Apex class or trigger that uses it", implying Salesforce permits the change and the code breaks afterwards. Considerations for Converting the Field Type of a Custom Field says the platform refuses the change while the reference exists: "You can't change the data type of a custom field referenced by other items in Setup such as Visualforce pages, Apex code, processes, or flows." Same answer, opposite sequence of events, and the corrected version explains why the stem's "cannot modify any Apex code" constraint is what makes A the answer. Also tightened B, which the earlier note described as being about "reportability of encrypted data"; the documented rule is that an existing field cannot be converted into an encrypted field at all.

question: An app builder notices several Accounts converted from Leads are missing information they expected to be caught via Account validation rules. What could be the source of this issue?
optionA: The Lead Settings option to require validation rules and triggers for converted leads is unchecked.
optionB: Account validation rules fail to validate on records converted from a lead.
optionC: The Lead Settings are allowing users to intentionally bypass validation rules.
optionD: Lead validation rules fail to validate on records when they are being converted.
explanation:
The Lead Settings option to require validation rules and triggers for converted leads being unchecked is the source. Lead Settings includes a checkbox, Require Validation for Converted Leads; if it is unchecked, validation rules on Account, Contact and Opportunity are skipped during lead conversion, allowing records that would not otherwise pass validation to be created.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Account validation rules never validate converted records) — they do, once the setting is on.
Option C (Lead Settings let users intentionally bypass validation) — the bypass is a system-wide setting, not a user choice.
Option D (Lead validation rules fail during conversion) — the missing information is on the Account, so the rules in question are Account rules, not Lead rules.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.fields_validation_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks's management team frequently travels and wants to approve requests from their team on the go via Chatter. Where would an app builder enable this ability?
optionA: Chatter Feed Tracking
optionC: Chatter Settings
explanation:
Chatter Settings is where the app builder enables it. The Allow Approvals option — Approvals in Chatter — is enabled in Setup under Chatter Settings; with it on, approval requests can be posted to Chatter and managers can approve or reject from the feed.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Chatter Feed Tracking) — controls which field changes post to the feed; it does not enable approvals.
Option B (Object Settings) — no such approval switch lives there.
Option D (Approval Process Settings) — the approval process itself can be set to post to Chatter, but only after the org-wide setting under Chatter Settings is on.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.approvals_for_chatter_enabling.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers wants to match Opportunity data from Salesforce to the records in a financial database. What is required to configure an indirect lookup relationship in Salesforce between the Salesforce Opportunity records and those in a financial database?
optionA: Salesforce Record ID
optionC: External ID and Unique custom field on the parent (Salesforce) object
explanation:
An External ID and Unique custom field on the parent Salesforce object is what an indirect lookup requires. An indirect lookup relationship matches an external object's child records to a Salesforce parent using a custom field on the parent that has both the External ID and Unique attributes; the external object's indirect-lookup field stores the matching key.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Salesforce Record ID) — the financial database does not hold Salesforce IDs; an indirect lookup exists precisely to match on a key the external system does have.
Option B (TEXT(Id)) — a formula expression, not a matching field.
Option D (CASESAFEID(Id)) — the same; a formula function, not a relationship configuration.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.custom_field_types.htm&type=5&language=en_US

question: The CFO of Cloud Kicks needs a way for new vendors to accept terms on agreements for any new major retail store lease before the opportunity can be closed. Which feature should be used to handle this requirement?
optionA: Email Alert
optionC: Approval Process
explanation:
An Approval Process is the feature. It can require vendor acceptance and sign-off as a step that must be completed before the opportunity is allowed to close.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Email Alert) — sends a notification; it enforces no sign-off gate.
Option B (Dynamic Action) — controls which actions show on a page; nothing to do with acceptance.
Option D (Validation Rule) — can block a save, but it cannot model a sign-off by an external party.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.approvals_automated_actions.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.what_are_approvals.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An app builder wants to deploy a new version of an autolaunched flow to production in an active state so that the new functionality is immediately available to users. What should the app builder take into consideration when planning the deployment?
optionA: Verify there is an Apex test that provides test coverage for the flow.
optionB: Grant user access to the flow.
optionC: Manually activate the flow after deployment.
optionD: Include the Process Builder calling the flow in the deployment.
explanation:
Verifying there is an Apex test that provides test coverage for the flow is the planning consideration. Deploying a flow as active is not the default behaviour, so two things have to be true. First, the org has to allow it: 'By default, processes and flows that are active in a sandbox or non-production org are deployed to a production org as inactive.' To change that, in Process Automation Settings you select Deploy processes and flows as active and enter a flow test coverage percentage. Second, the coverage bar has to be met: 'Before you can deploy a process or autolaunched flow as active, make sure you meet flow test coverage requirements. At least one Apex test must cover the flow test coverage percentage of the active processes and autolaunched flows.' It applies to autolaunched flows, which is what this stem describes; flows with screens are exempt.
Be careful with the threshold. The number is whatever percentage the org has configured in Process Automation Settings, not a fixed platform figure, and it is a distinct requirement from the Apex code coverage rule that governs deployments generally.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (grant user access to the flow) — an autolaunched flow runs without a user launching it; access is not what gates active deployment.
Option C (manually activate after deployment) — exactly the default outcome the requirement is trying to avoid; manual reactivation is what happens when the active-deployment setting is off.
Option D (include the calling Process Builder) — nothing in the stem says a process calls the flow, and Process Builder is past end of support.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_distribute_deploy_active.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Key A stands, but the explanation asserted a number the documentation does not: it claimed deploying an active flow 'requires at least 75% Apex test coverage in the org just like any deployment'. The word 75 does not appear on the Deploy Processes and Flows as Active page at all. What it documents is a configurable flow test coverage percentage, entered in Process Automation Settings, with the requirement that 'at least one Apex test must cover the flow test coverage percentage' — a separate mechanism from the Apex code coverage rule the old text borrowed the figure from. Rewritten to name the real mechanism, to add the prerequisite setting that the old explanation omitted entirely, and to record that screen flows are exempt.

question: Universal Containers (UC) has large data volumes and is nearing data storage limits. The planned solution is to archive historical data to reduce data storage in Salesforce; however, UC would still like to use reports, queries, and lookups on the archived information. Which two options could meet this requirement? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Big Objects
optionC: Related Objects
explanation:
Big Objects and External Objects are the two options. Both keep large volumes of data reportable without consuming standard Salesforce data storage. A big object 'stores and manages massive amounts of data on the Salesforce platform', and archiving from other objects into one is a documented use — 'You can archive data from other objects or bring massive datasets from outside systems into a big object'. External objects take the other route: through Salesforce Connect they surface records that remain in the external system, so nothing is copied into Salesforce at all.
One important currency correction on how you get data back out of a big object. Async SOQL is no longer the answer: Salesforce retired it with the Summer '23 release, stating 'You must use the Bulk API or batch Apex to query or report on custom Big Objects'. CRM Analytics still loads big object data, using Bulk API requests. Also keep the trade-off in view: big objects are built for scale rather than for interactive use, with no standard UI or list views and a deliberately narrow query surface, whereas external objects give live access but depend on the external system's availability.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Custom Objects) — would consume the very storage the project is trying to reclaim.
Option C (Related Objects) — not a Salesforce feature.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.bigobjects.meta/bigobjects/big_object.htm
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000394892&language=en_US&type=1

corrected.note: Key A,D stands, but the explanation cited a retired capability. It justified Big Objects by saying they support 'async SOQL/queries' — Salesforce retired Async SOQL for Big Objects with Summer '23, almost three years before this deck was reviewed, and now directs you to Bulk API or batch Apex to query or report on them. Rewritten to name the current mechanism and to be honest about the trade-off the old text waved at with 'some limitations': big objects have no standard UI or list views and a narrow query surface, so they are archival storage with code-based retrieval rather than a drop-in reporting source.

question: Universal Containers would like to embed a chart of all related Opportunities, by stage, on the Account detail page. Which type of report should the app builder create to add to the Account page layout?
optionA: A summary report on the Opportunity object.
optionB: A summary report on the Account object.
optionC: A tabular report on the Account object.
optionD: A tabular report on the Opportunity object.
explanation:
A summary report on the Opportunity object is what the app builder should create. To embed a chart on a record page the report must be a summary, matrix or joined report — tabular reports cannot have charts — and it must filter by the parent record; a summary report on Opportunity grouped by Stage produces the chart on the related Account.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (summary report on Account) — the chart is of Opportunities by stage, so the report must be built on Opportunity, not Account.
Option C (tabular report on Account) — tabular reports cannot carry a chart, and the object is wrong.
Option D (tabular report on Opportunity) — the right object, but a tabular report cannot have a chart.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.reports_embed_pagelayout.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks (CK) wants to simultaneously delete a Supplier's record and all SupplierItem__c records if a partnership ends with a supplier. What solution could an app builder use to meet the requirement?
optionA: Many-to-many
optionC: Hierarchical
explanation:
A Master-detail relationship is the solution. Master-detail relationships cascade delete: when the parent Supplier is deleted, all detail SupplierItem__c records are automatically deleted with it.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Many-to-many) — a junction between two masters; a Supplier and its items are one-to-many.
Option B (Indirect lookup) — relates an external object to a Salesforce object; no cascade delete.
Option C (Hierarchical) — available only on the User object.
References:
