DR executives want to automate the submission of travel request forms to enforce the internal policy. How should an app builder automate travel requests based on these criteria?
optionA: Process Builder
optionC: Approval process
explanation:
An approval process is how the app builder should automate travel requests. It is the natural fit for requests requiring policy-driven sign-off: define entry criteria, route to the appropriate approvers, and capture the approve or reject decision with an audit trail.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Process Builder) — could submit a request but cannot itself model the sign-off, and is past end of support.
Option B (workflow rule) — can notify or update a field; it records no decision, and is past end of support.
Option D (Apex) — code for something the platform provides declaratively.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.what_are_approvals.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.approvals_step_approver.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The Universal Containers data manager has been complaining about the lack of data integrity on Contact records. Sales reps have not been filling out the Region field. The data manager wants the Region field filled out only for Contacts that are associated to Accounts that have been marked as 'High Priority' on the Customer Status field. What can the app builder do to fulfill this requirement?
optionA: Make the Region field required on Contact.
optionB: Create a validation rule on Contact.
optionC: Create a validation rule on Account.
optionD: Make the Customer Status field required on Account.
explanation:
Creating a validation rule on Contact is what the app builder can do. A rule such as AND(ISPICKVAL(Account.Customer_Status__c, 'High Priority'), ISBLANK(Region__c)) enforces the conditional requirement based on the parent Account's Customer Status — something a layout-level Required setting cannot do.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (make Region required on Contact) — unconditional; it would require Region for every contact, not only those on High Priority accounts.
Option C (a validation rule on Account) — the field being enforced is on Contact, and an Account rule cannot inspect its contacts' fields.
Option D (make Customer Status required on Account) — ensures the status is filled in; it does nothing about Region.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_field_validation.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_creating_cross_object_notes.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: AW Computing has a custom object for service plans. A service plan needs to be associated to one and only one contact. The support manager noticed if the wrong contact is associated, the reps are unable to change the contact. The app builder already confirmed the user has correct access to the field and there are no validations associated with the service plans. What could be causing the issue?
optionA: The Read Only radio button — Allows users with at least Read access to the master record to create, edit, or delete related detail records — is selected.
optionB: The Allow Reparenting checkbox — Child records can be reparented to other parent records after they are created — is unchecked.
optionC: The Read/Write radio button — Allows users with at least Read/Write access to the master record to create, edit, or delete related detail records — is selected.
optionD: The Allow Reparenting checkbox — Child records can be reparented to other parent records after they are created — is checked.
explanation:
The Allow Reparenting checkbox being unchecked is what is causing the issue. In a master-detail relationship, Allow Reparenting must be enabled to let the parent of an existing detail record be changed; with it unchecked — the default — the relationship field on the detail record is effectively locked once set, exactly matching the symptom.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Read Only sharing setting selected) — governs whether users with Read on the master can create, edit or delete details; the user already has correct access, and this setting does not lock the parent field.
Option C (Read/Write sharing setting selected) — the same setting, the other value; not what locks reparenting.
Option D (Allow Reparenting checked) — the opposite: checked would let the reps change the contact.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.overview_of_custom_object_relationships.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.relationships_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An app builder has deployed a change set from a sandbox to production. There is a long delay in the deployment. What can be causing the delay?
optionA: Profiles are included in the change set.
optionB: A field type change is included in the change set.
optionC: Dependent fields are included in the change set.
optionD: Roles are included in the change set.
explanation:
A field type change included in the change set is what can be causing the delay. A field type change is not a metadata edit that lands instantly; it is a data conversion over every existing record. Salesforce documents both the behaviour and the scale: 'When you change a custom field data type, the conversion runs in the background. The conversion can take a while depending on the size of the custom field, the number of records affected, and the type of field conversion. In some cases, the conversion can take over 24 hours to complete.' Picklist to Text, Text to Picklist, Date/Time to Time and Time to Text are called out as the slowest. The same page ties this to deployments specifically: a deployment that changes field data types on objects holding a lot of data can fail against a ceiling of 85 million field type conversions — 30 million records with three text-to-picklist changes is 90 million conversions, over the limit.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (profiles in the change set) — makes the change set larger and fiddlier to assemble but involves no per-record work.
Option C (dependent fields) — picklist dependencies are a metadata relationship that deploys as metadata.
Option D (roles) — the same as profiles: metadata only, no per-record conversion.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.notes_on_changing_custom_field_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.changesets_inbound_deploy.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Key B stands. The explanation was rewritten to replace an unsourced mechanism with the documented one: it had claimed the delay comes from scanning every record 'plus revalidate dependent metadata (formulas, validation rules, Apex)', which the article doesn't say. What it does say is that the conversion runs in the background and 'in some cases... can take over 24 hours to complete', and that a deployment changing field data types on large objects hits a limit of 85 million field type conversions. Those two facts settle the item without inventing a mechanism.

question: The app builder at Ursa Major Solar has just created a master-detail relationship between a parent object Galaxy__c and child object Star__c. What would be the effect of creating this type of relationship if users want to report on Galaxy__c with Star__c?
optionA: A Star__c report type with Galaxy__c as a field will be automatically created.
optionB: A new custom report type will need to be created for Star__c with lookup fields from Galaxy__c.
optionC: A Galaxy__c with Star__c report type will be automatically created.
optionD: A new custom report type will need to be created for Galaxy__c with Star__c.
explanation:
A "Galaxy__c with Star__c" report type will be automatically created. When a master-detail relationship is created between two custom objects, Salesforce automatically generates a standard report type of the form Parent with Child — here, Galaxies with Stars — so users can immediately report on parents joined with their children.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (a Star__c report type with Galaxy__c as a field) — the auto-generated type is parent-with-child, not child-with-parent-field; the parent's fields are available on the Star report type as lookup fields, but that is not the joined report type the question describes.
Option B (a new custom report type for Star__c with lookup fields) — unnecessary; the standard type is created for you.
Option D (a new custom report type for Galaxy__c with Star__c) — unnecessary for the same reason.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000383026&language=en_US&type=1
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.overview_of_custom_object_relationships.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An app builder creates an Account validation rule on the Industry field that will throw an error if the length of the field is longer than 6 characters. Another app builder creates a workflow rule with a field update that sets the Industry field to 'Technology' whenever the Billing City field is set to 'San Francisco'. What will happen the next time a salesperson saves an Account with a Billing City of San Francisco?
optionA: The record will save and the Industry field will change to Technology.
optionB: The record will not save and the validation rule's error message will be displayed.
optionC: The record will not save and no error message will be displayed.
optionD: The record will save but the Industry field will not change to Technology.
explanation:
The record will save and the Industry field will change to Technology. A workflow field update does not re-run custom validation rules, so the 10-character value the update writes is never tested against the rule that would have rejected it. The order of execution settles this: custom validation rules run before the record is saved, against the values the salesperson entered — at that point Billing City is San Francisco and the rule has nothing to complain about. When a workflow field update then changes the record, Salesforce 'updates the record again' and 'runs system validations again' — but 'custom validation rules, flows, duplicate rules, processes built with Process Builder, and escalation rules aren't run again'. Salesforce states the consequence outright: 'Workflow rules and some processes can invalidate previously valid fields.'
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (does not save, validation error shown) — the intuitive answer and the reason this item exists; it would be right only if the user had typed Technology themselves, because then the value would be present when custom validation ran.
Option C (does not save, no error) — a failed save always surfaces its error; and the save does not fail.
Option D (saves but Industry does not change) — the field update runs after the save and writes Technology.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_triggers_order_of_execution.htm
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.workflow_field_update_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Answer moved B to A. Two independent official sources agree and neither is ambiguous. Triggers and Order of Execution, step by step: 'Executes workflow rules. If there are workflow field updates: Updates the record again. Runs system validations again. Custom validation rules, flows, duplicate rules, processes built with Process Builder, and escalation rules aren't run again.' And Considerations for Field Update Actions: 'Workflow rules and some processes can invalidate previously valid fields. Invalidation occurs because updates to records based on workflow rules and also on process-scheduled actions don't trigger validation rules.' The deck's explanation had the order backwards, asserting that 'validation rules run after workflow field updates re-evaluate'. Custom validation rules have not re-run after workflow field updates for well over a decade, which is why orgs accumulate records that violate their own validation rules. The record saves and Industry becomes Technology.

question: An app builder is creating a Lightning record page and has added Mobile & Lightning Actions to the page layout. What two components could be included on the Lightning record page to display the actions? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Highlights Panel
optionC: Activities
explanation:
The Highlights Panel and the Activities component are the two components that display the actions. Actions added to the Salesforce Mobile and Lightning Experience Actions section of a page layout surface in specific components, and Salesforce enumerates them. The Highlights Panel is the main one: "The actions in the highlights panel come from the Salesforce Mobile and Lightning Experience Actions section of the page layout." The Activities component is the second — Salesforce notes that the activity-related actions are deliberately routed there: "The component can contain Create a Record quick actions that point to the Event and Task objects. It contains Log A Call and Send Email actions." The worked example in Actions in Lightning Experience makes the split explicit: "New Event and New Task don't show up here", in the page-level menu, and instead "The Activities-related actions - Email, New Event, New Task - display on the Activity tab."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Report Chart) — a display component that renders a chart from a report; it hosts no actions from the page layout.
Option D (Path) — displays no actions at all; a path is built from picklist steps, key fields and guidance for success.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.actions_in_lex.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.lightning_page_components.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.path_create.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note:
Answer moved A,D to A,C. D is unsupported: Actions in Lightning Experience enumerates every place actions appear on a record page - the highlights panel's page-level action menu, the Activity tab, and the Chatter tab - and Path appears nowhere in it. The Path setup documentation contains no occurrence of the word 'action' at all; a path consists of steps, key fields and guidance text. The deck's explanation asserted that 'The Path component also exposes layout actions associated with each step', which nothing documents. C is documented twice over, in the Standard Lightning Page Components entry for Activities and in the worked example showing New Event and New Task moving off the highlights panel onto the Activity tab. Flagging one soft edge for the user: B is partly true as well, since the Chatter tab carries the standard Chatter actions from the same page-layout section, so this item has three options with some claim and one with none. A,C is the pair the documentation supports for the quick actions an app builder would be adding.

Follow-up on the same day: option B originally read "Chatter", which was a soft edge rather than a clean distractor - the Chatter tab does carry the standard Chatter actions (Post, Poll, Question, Announcement) from the same page-layout section, so a reader could defend it. B has been replaced with "Report Chart", a display component that hosts no actions, leaving exactly two correct options. Treat the new option B as authored, not original.

question: Which two places can an app builder go to see a list of available custom Lightning components in their org? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Visualforce Components in Setup
optionC: Lightning App Builder
explanation:
Lightning App Builder and Lightning Components in Setup are the two places. Setup > Lightning Components lists all custom Lightning (Aura and LWC) components in the org, and Lightning App Builder surfaces them in the Components panel under Custom when editing a page.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Visualforce Components in Setup) — lists Visualforce components, a different technology.
Option B (Lightning Component Generator) — not a Salesforce feature.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/use-setup.html
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.lightning_page_components.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Northern Trail Outfitters wants the field sales team to only see the accounts that they own. Separate North American and European marketing teams should only see accounts in their respective regions. The inside sales team needs to see all accounts in Salesforce. How can this be accomplished?
optionA: Set the Organization-Wide Default to Public for accounts. Create criteria-based sharing rules for each marketing team, and create an Inside Sales Team permission set with the View All setting for accounts.
optionB: Set the Organization-Wide Default to Public for accounts. Create profiles for each marketing team, and create an Inside Sales Team role that is at the top of the role hierarchy.
optionC: Set the Organization-Wide Default to Private for accounts. Create criteria-based sharing rules for each marketing team, and create an Inside Sales Team profile (or permission set) with the View All setting for accounts.
optionD: Set the Organization-Wide Default to Private for accounts. Create permission sets for each marketing team, and create an Inside Sales Team profile with the View All setting for accounts.
explanation:
Setting the org-wide default to Private, creating criteria-based sharing rules for each marketing team, and giving Inside Sales a profile or permission set with View All on accounts is how it is accomplished. Private OWD restricts field sales to records they own; criteria-based sharing rules grant each marketing team access to records matching their region; View All lets Inside Sales see every Account regardless of OWD or sharing rules.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (OWD Public) — a public default lets the field sales team see every account, which the requirement forbids.
Option B (OWD Public, profiles per marketing team, a top-of-hierarchy role) — the same public-default problem, and profiles do not scope record access by region.
Option D (permission sets per marketing team) — permission sets grant object and field permissions, not regional record access; sharing rules are the mechanism.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.managing_the_sharing_model.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.security_sharing_rules_criteria.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.users_profiles_view_all_mod_all.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: DreamHouse Realty wants to display a weather map component on a Lightning record page when a house is scheduled for a showing. How should the app builder meet the requirement?
optionA: Component visibility
optionC: Field-level field
explanation:
Component visibility is how the app builder meets the requirement. Lightning App Builder's component visibility rules conditionally show or hide a component based on field values, user attributes or device type; setting visibility on the weather component to show when a showing is scheduled meets it declaratively.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (field-level security) — controls who can see a field, not whether a page component renders.
Option C (field-level field) — not a Salesforce feature.
Option D (sharing rules) — control record access, not component display.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.lightning_page_components_visibility.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.lightning_page_components_visibility_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The sales operations team at AW Computing deletes accounts for a variety of reasons. The sales ops director is worried that the sales team may delete accounts that sales reps are actively selling into. How should the app builder keep accounts with open opportunities from being deleted?
optionA: Create an Apex trigger on the Account object.
optionB: Create a validation rule on the Account object.
optionC: Remove the Delete button on the account layout.
optionD: Remove the Delete permission from the Sales Rep profile.
explanation:
Creating an Apex trigger on the Account object is how to keep accounts with open opportunities from being deleted. Validation rules never run on a delete, so that leaves a mechanism that can inspect the account's related opportunities at delete time and refuse — a before-delete Apex trigger that queries for open Opportunities and calls addError() on the offending accounts.
Worth knowing beyond the four options: this no longer has to be code. A record-triggered flow configured to run before a record is deleted can use a Custom Error element, which Salesforce documents as using 'the same functionality as the addError() method in Apex' and describes with this exact scenario. A declarative build is the one to reach for first today; Apex remains the answer here because no flow option is offered.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (a validation rule on Account) — validation rules never run on a delete, so no formula can express the requirement.
Option C (remove the Delete button) — unconditional, and it hides one route to deletion while leaving the API, list views and mass delete open.
Option D (remove Delete from the Sales Rep profile) — unconditional too: it stops the team deleting any account, including the many with no open opportunities that sales operations legitimately clears out.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_ref_elements_custom_error.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_triggers_order_of_execution.htm

corrected.note: Key A stands - it is the only workable option offered - but the explanation called an Apex trigger 'the appropriate solution', which is no longer true in general. The Custom Error element, usable in the before-save or after-save path of a record-triggered flow, blocks a deletion declaratively and is documented with this precise use case: 'Use the Custom Error element to roll back a change that triggered a flow and inform the user exactly what caused the error... For example, when a user deletes a record that triggers a flow, the flow can return an error message that tells the user why the deletion wasn't allowed.' The article also notes that a few objects, such as OpportunityTeamMember and CampaignMember, don't support custom errors on before-delete. Account is not among them.

question: Cloud Kicks wants to make sure that users without the Marketing role are unable to update the Contact Retail Opt In picklist field to 'Yes'. What validation rule would an app builder use to prevent other users from making this update?
optionA: AND( $UserRole.Name != 'Marketing', ISCHANGED(Retail_Opt_In__c), ISPICKVAL(Retail_Opt_In__c, 'Yes') )
optionC: AND( $UserRole.Name = 'Marketing', ISPICKVAL(Retail_Opt_In__c, 'Yes') )
explanation:
AND( $UserRole.Name != 'Marketing', ISCHANGED(Retail_Opt_In__c), ISPICKVAL(Retail_Opt_In__c, 'Yes') ) is the validation rule. It fires when the user is not in the Marketing role, the field is being changed, and the new value is Yes. ISPICKVAL is required because Retail Opt In is a picklist — picklists cannot be compared with = — and ISCHANGED prevents the rule from blocking saves where the field already held Yes and is unchanged.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B ($UserRole.Name != 'Marketing', Retail_Opt_In__c = 'Yes') — compares a picklist with =, which is a syntax error, and without ISCHANGED it would block every save of an already-opted-in contact by a non-Marketing user.
Option C ($UserRole.Name = 'Marketing', ISPICKVAL(..., 'Yes')) — inverted: it blocks the Marketing role, the one group allowed to make the update.
Option D ($UserRole.Name = 'Marketing', Retail_Opt_In__c = 'Yes') — inverted and syntactically invalid.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.tips_for_using_picklist_formula_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_validation_rules_tips.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.customize_functions_ischanged.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Shipments at Cloud Kicks (CK) are created and updated by the warehouse staff in a shipping application. The information needs to be pushed into Salesforce on a regular basis. CK's app builder creates a custom object called Delivery__c to track the information. How can the app builder prevent creating duplicate delivery records and update the correct existing records when migrating data from the shipping application?
optionA: Use the Import Wizard and match on the tracking number.
optionB: Create a unique External ID field and use Data Loader.
optionC: Use the Import Wizard and match on the Salesforce ID.
optionD: Create a duplicate match rule and use Data Loader.
explanation:
Creating a unique External ID field and using Data Loader is how to prevent duplicates and update the right records. Add a custom field on Delivery__c with both External ID and Unique attributes that holds the shipping app's record key, then use Data Loader's Upsert operation against that External ID to update existing records and insert only true new ones — the canonical pattern for recurring external integrations.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Import Wizard matching on tracking number) — the Import Wizard does not support custom objects with arbitrary match fields at the scale of a recurring integration, and it cannot be scheduled.
Option C (Import Wizard matching on Salesforce ID) — the shipping application does not know Salesforce IDs.
Option D (a duplicate match rule with Data Loader) — duplicate rules can block or alert on inserts; they do not route an update to the correct existing record.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.custom_field_attributes.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.dataLoader.meta/dataLoader/when_to_use_the_data_loader.htm

question: The Recruiting team at AW Computing captures the job acceptance and date of hire of a candidate on the Job Application custom object. Once the candidate accepts the recruiter's job offer, the date of hire should be entered and not be changed on subsequent record edits. Which validation formula should the app builder use?
optionA: NOT(ISBLANK(Job_Accepted__c)) && ISCHANGED(Hire_Date__c)
optionC: NOT(ISBLANK(Job_Accepted__c)) || ISCHANGED(Hire_Date__c)
explanation:
NOT(ISBLANK(Job_Accepted__c)) && ISCHANGED(Hire_Date__c) is the validation formula. A validation rule fires — and blocks the save — when its formula evaluates to TRUE, so the formula has to describe the forbidden situation: the offer has been accepted, and the hire date is being changed. Only this option joins them with AND.
One limitation to understand before copying this rule into an org. ISCHANGED returns FALSE when evaluating any field on a newly created record, so the rule governs edits only. Combined with the AND, the hire date is effectively writable on the record's initial save and locked from then on: entering it for the first time in a later edit, after acceptance has been recorded, is also blocked. A production version would need to allow the transition from blank to a value — for example by adding NOT(ISBLANK(PRIORVALUE(Hire_Date__c))) — so that only changes to an already-set date are rejected. As printed, A is still the only defensible answer of the four.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (ISBLANK(Job_Accepted__c) || NOT(ISCHANGED(...))) — starts from the applications where no offer has been accepted, the opposite population, and fires on ordinary saves where the date is unchanged.
Option C (NOT(ISBLANK(...)) || ISCHANGED(...)) — uses OR, so it blocks every edit to an accepted application whether or not the hire date moved.
Option D (ISBLANK(...) && NOT(ISCHANGED(...))) — fires on unaccepted applications whose hire date is not changed, blocking ordinary saves on the wrong records.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_validation_rules_tips.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.customize_functions_ischanged.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.customize_functions_priorvalue.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Key A stands and the item is sound as a formula-reading question; the explanation was extended rather than corrected. It previously stopped at "Option A is the only formula that combines both conditions correctly with AND", which is true but leaves a reader thinking the rule is production-ready. It is not: ISCHANGED "returns FALSE when evaluating any field on a newly created record", so with the AND the field is writable on insert and frozen afterwards, and the first entry of a hire date after acceptance is blocked along with genuine changes. The explanation now says so and names the PRIORVALUE guard that fixes it. Decision recorded: the repo owner chose to leave the key and options untouched and surface the caveat in the prose.

question: Cloud Kicks wants to display the number of opportunities that are Closed Won with a Close Date within the last year on the Account detail page. Which tool should an app builder use to implement this?
optionA: Process Builder
optionC: Roll-Up Summary Field
explanation:
A Roll-Up Summary Field on Account is the tool, and it works here because of a documented exception rather than the general rule. Roll-up summary fields normally require the summarised records to sit on the detail side of a master-detail relationship, which Opportunity is not; Salesforce nonetheless allows them in a short list of standard cases, and 'Accounts using the values of related opportunities' is one of them — alongside Opportunities rolling up opportunity products and Campaigns rolling up campaign members. So create a COUNT roll-up on Account over Opportunity and use the roll-up's filter criteria to limit it to stage Closed Won with a close date inside the window.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Process Builder) — cannot aggregate child records, and reached end of support on 31 December 2025.
Option B (Activity Timeline) — lists tasks, events and logged calls on a record; it neither counts opportunities nor produces a field.
Option D (Workflow Rule) — cannot aggregate either, and reached end of support on the same date.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_roll_up_summary_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_defining_summary_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks wants to summarize the number of open Cases related to an Account, as well as the number of closed Cases to indicate whether customer support utilization is high, medium, or low. Two number fields have been created: NUM_Open_Cases__c and NUM_Closed_Cases__c. Which two automation solutions would meet these business requirements? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: AppExchange
optionC: Approval Process
explanation:
AppExchange and Apex are the two automation solutions. Apex triggers on Case can recalculate and write the open and closed counts to the parent Account when Cases are created, updated or deleted, and AppExchange offers prebuilt lookup roll-up and declarative roll-up summary apps that handle this without custom code — needed because Account to Case is a lookup, so a native roll-up summary is unavailable.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Validation Rule) — blocks saves; it computes no aggregate and writes no field.
Option C (Approval Process) — routes records for sign-off; it counts nothing.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_roll_up_summary_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.distribution_installing_packages.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Sales reps at Cloud Kicks (CK) forget to submit for approval when CK needs orders reviewed before Closed Won. CK wants to automatically submit opportunities into the Secure Commitment stage to eliminate manual submission. Which feature meets the business requirements?
optionA: Record-Triggered Flow optimized for Fast Field Updates
optionC: Platform Event-Triggered Flow
optionD: Record-Triggered Flow optimized for Actions and Related Records
explanation:
A Record-Triggered Flow optimized for Actions and Related Records is the feature. Submitting a record for approval is an action, not a same-record field update, so the flow must use the Actions and Related Records (after-save) optimization.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Fast Field Updates) — a before-save flow can only set fields on the triggering record; it cannot invoke Submit for Approval.
Option B (custom button and screen flow) — still requires a rep to click, which is the manual submission the requirement eliminates.
Option C (Platform Event-Triggered Flow) — fires on a published event, not on an opportunity reaching a stage.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_concepts_trigger_record.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_ref_elements_actions_approval.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which three options are available when activating a Lightning page from the Lightning App Builder? Choose 3 answers.
optionA: Assign the page to a combination of apps and profiles.
optionB: Assign the page to a combination of apps and permission sets.
optionC: Make the page the org default.
optionD: Make the page the default home page for specific roles.
optionE: Make the page the default home page for specific apps.
explanation:
Assigning the page to a combination of apps and profiles, making it the org default, and making it the default for specific apps are the three activation options. Activation supports assignment by app and profile combination, org default for that page type, and app default; assignment is by profile, not by role or permission set.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (apps and permission sets) — activation does not assign by permission set.
Option D (default home page for specific roles) — activation does not assign by role.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.lightning_app_builder_customize_lex_pages_activate.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An app builder needs to create new automation on an object. What best practice should the app builder follow when building out automation?
optionA: One workflow rule per object.
optionC: One invocable process per object.
optionD: One record-triggered flow per object per trigger context.
explanation:
One record-triggered flow per object per trigger context is the best practice. Salesforce's guidance is to consolidate automation per object per trigger context — one before-save record-triggered flow and one after-save record-triggered flow per object — so ordering is predictable and the recursion and conflict issues that come with many overlapping automations on the same object are avoided.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (one workflow rule per object) — workflow is past end of support, and one rule cannot express the automation an object typically needs.
Option B (one flow per object) — too coarse: before-save and after-save contexts have different capabilities and should be separate flows.
Option C (one invocable process per object) — Process Builder is past end of support.
References:
https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/decision-guides/guide/record-triggered.html
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_concepts_trigger_record.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A sales manager at Cloud Kicks wants the team to spend more time in the field and less time manually entering the information found on the business cards they collect. What should an app builder do to help achieve this goal without sacrificing data quality?
optionA: Research and evaluate data enrichment products on the AppExchange to automate data entry.
optionB: Post daily to the Chatter feed any relevant fields that need to be populated.
optionC: Use Flow to create a data entry wizard to automate data entry.
optionD: Use a combination of workflow rules and formula fields to populate key fields for the sales user.
explanation:
Researching and evaluating data enrichment products on the AppExchange to automate data entry is what the app builder should do. Business-card-scanning and data-enrichment apps automate the OCR and extraction step and populate Salesforce records with verified data, reducing manual entry without compromising quality; internal automations cannot read business cards on their own.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (daily Chatter posts about fields to populate) — reminders, not automation; the reps still type everything.
Option C (a Flow data entry wizard) — still manual entry, arranged differently.
Option D (workflow rules and formula fields) — can derive values from data already entered; they cannot capture what is on a card.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.distribution_installing_packages.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks (CK) is finding sales reps are inconsistent in data entry when deals are won. CK requires that custom shoes are shipped within two weeks after the close date. A custom field called Scheduled Ship Date on the opportunity records the ship date. How should the app builder ensure this field is properly filled out before setting the opportunity to Closed Won?
optionA: OR( ISPICKVAL(StageName, 'Closed Won') && (Scheduled_Ship_Date__c - CloseDate) > 14, AND(ISPICKVAL(StageName, 'Closed Won'), ISBLANK(Scheduled_Ship_Date__c)) )
optionC: ISPICKVAL(StageName, 'Closed Won') && (Scheduled_Ship_Date__c - CloseDate) > 14
explanation:
OR( ISPICKVAL(StageName, 'Closed Won') && (Scheduled_Ship_Date__c - CloseDate) > 14, AND(ISPICKVAL(StageName, 'Closed Won'), ISBLANK(Scheduled_Ship_Date__c)) ) is the rule. It fires on Closed Won when either the ship date is more than 14 days after the close date or the ship date is blank, and it uses ISPICKVAL correctly for the picklist comparison.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (ISPICKVAL(StageName = 'Closed Won') ... OR ISBLANK(...)) — invalid syntax: = inside ISPICKVAL; and the blank test is not gated on Closed Won, so it would block every open opportunity without a ship date.
Option C (Closed Won and more than 14 days only) — checks only one of the two conditions; a blank ship date passes.
Option D (ISPICKVAL(StageName = 'Closed Won') && (CloseDate - Scheduled_Ship_Date__c) > 14) — invalid syntax, and the subtraction is reversed.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.tips_for_using_picklist_formula_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_validation_rules_tips.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: What is one limitation of using Schema Builder when creating a field?
optionA: Cannot create formula fields.
optionB: Cannot see existing relationships between objects.
optionC: Cannot add fields to page layouts.
explanation:
Not being able to add fields to page layouts is the limitation. Schema Builder creates fields but does not add them to any page layout; that step must be done in the page layout editor (or on the Lightning record page in App Builder) afterwards.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (cannot create formula fields) — Schema Builder can create formula fields.
Option B (cannot see existing relationships) — visualising relationships is Schema Builder's main purpose.
Option D (cannot create lookup relationships) — it creates lookup and master-detail relationships.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.schema_builder_elements_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.schema_builder_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers has two types of applicants, hourly and salary. There are separate record types for each. While all members of the Human Resources department need to be able to view all applicant records, only the Hiring Manager and VP of HR should be able to create salary applicant records. What should the app builder recommend to meet this requirement?
optionA: Update the org-wide default to private and create a sharing rule for the role of Recruiting Manager.
optionB: Create a permission set containing the Salary record type and assign it to the appropriate users.
optionC: Remove Create permission for the Salary applicant object for everyone except the manager and VP.
optionD: Configure the Hourly record type as the default and instruct non-management users to accept the default record type.
explanation:
Creating a permission set containing the Salary record type and assigning it to the appropriate users is the recommendation. Record types are assigned through profiles or permission sets; a permission set granting the Salary record type, assigned only to the Hiring Manager and VP of HR, restricts who can create Salary applicant records while leaving everyone's read access intact.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (private OWD with a sharing rule) — sharing controls who sees records, not which record types a user may create, and it would break HR's view-all requirement.
Option C (remove Create on the Salary applicant object) — there is one Applicant object with two record types, so object-level Create cannot be removed for one type.
Option D (Hourly as the default and instruct users) — an instruction is not a control; non-management users could still pick Salary.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.perm_sets_record_types_assign.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.permissions_record_type_access.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks has Leads owned by users and queues. The sales manager wants the status to change to 'Working' when a user takes ownership. What does an app builder need to have in the criteria to ensure the process runs without error?
optionA: BEGINS([Lead].OwnerId, '005')
optionC: [Lead].Owner:Queue.OwnerId Is Null = True
explanation:
BEGINS([Lead].OwnerId, '005') is what the criteria need. A lead's OwnerId can hold either a user or a queue, and the two are different kinds of record; testing the ID's key prefix is the safe way to tell them apart, since every user ID begins with 005, so the expression is true only when a person has taken ownership — exactly the moment the status should move to Working.
One note on tooling: the bracket syntax in these options is Process Builder criteria, and Salesforce ended support for Process Builder on 31 December 2025. Build this as a record-triggered flow on Lead instead, with an entry condition using the same prefix test on the Owner ID.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B ([Lead].Owner:User.Role Is Null = False) — reaches through the owner to a related User that does not exist when a queue owns the lead, so the criterion has nothing to resolve and errors.
Option C ([Lead].Owner:Queue.OwnerId Is Null = True) — the mirror problem: when a user owns the lead there is no related Queue.
Option D (NOT(ISBLANK([Lead].OwnerId))) — true for every lead ever saved, since OwnerId is required and never blank, so it fires on queue-owned leads too.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000385203&language=en_US&type=1
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000389396&language=en_US&type=1
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.customize_functions_text.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Key A stands. The prefix fact is confirmed by the Salesforce Entity Key Prefix Decoder, which states that 'The entity type of every Salesforce record ID is encoded in its first three characters, known as the key prefix' and lists User as 005; a queue-owned lead carries a Group ID instead, which does not match. The explanation was rewritten for two reasons: it presented the criteria as current Process Builder practice when support for Process Builder ended on 31 December 2025, and it left D unexplained. D fails on a simple fact rather than a subtle one - OwnerId is always populated, so NOT(ISBLANK(...)) is always true and would run the automation on queue-owned leads too.

question: DreamHouse Realty (DHR) recently acquired Cloud Kicks (CK), a company that is still on Salesforce Classic. DHR is keeping the CK Salesforce org; however, it will migrate this org to Lightning Experience. Where should the app builder find prebuilt resources to help with this project and overall adoption?
optionA: Import Wizard
optionC: AppExchange
explanation:
AppExchange is where the app builder should look. It hosts solution packs, Lightning Experience readiness apps, migration assistants and consulting partners built specifically to help orgs move from Classic to Lightning Experience and drive user adoption.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Import Wizard) — loads data; nothing to do with migrating an org's UI.
Option B (Lightning Object Creator) — builds a custom object from a spreadsheet.
Option D (Flow Builder) — builds automation, not migration resources.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.distribution_installing_packages.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers has created two custom objects called Seminars and Attendees. Organization-wide defaults for these objects have been set to Private. Universal Containers wants to set up a new junction object between these custom objects. A select group of users should be able to edit records in the junction object. Which two steps should an app builder take to configure the proper security? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Create owner-based sharing rules that give Read access to the master objects.
optionB: Set lookup filters on both junction object relationship fields.
optionC: Set Sharing Settings to Read Only on both Master-Detail relationship fields.
optionD: Create an owner-based sharing rule that gives Read access to the junction object.
explanation:
Owner-based sharing rules that give the group Read access to both master objects (option A), combined with the Read Only sharing setting on both master-detail relationship fields (option C), let the select group edit junction records. Custom Object Security spells out the mechanism: editing a detail record needs "Edit permission and either read or read/write access to the related master record, depending on the value of the Sharing Setting attribute of the master-detail relationship field", and for a junction object "the user must have read access to both master records." With the Sharing Setting at Read Only, Read on the masters is enough, and sharing rules are what open Private masters to a group.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Lookup filters on both relationship fields) — lookup filters restrict which records can be chosen in a lookup; they grant no access.
Option D (An owner-based sharing rule on the junction object) — a junction object's access is derived from its masters ("sharing access to a junction object record is determined by a user's sharing access to both associated master records"); sharing rules are not defined on the detail side.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.dev_security.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.relationships_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_sharing_rules_owner.htm&type=5&language=en_US

question: Universal Containers (UC) has several picklist fields on the Account object whose values are routinely modified to meet changing business requirements. Due to these revolving changes, UC has a high number of inactive picklist values that are impacting system performance and user experience. What can the app builder do to alleviate this issue?
optionA: Establish upper bound on existing picklists in Picklist Settings.
optionB: Set up Global Values in Picklist Value Sets.
optionC: Remove upper bound on inactive picklist values in Picklist Settings.
optionD: Convert the picklist fields to a different field type that will still meet the business requirements.
explanation:
Establishing an upper bound on the existing picklists in Picklist Settings is the documented remedy. Manage Inactive Picklist Values says it directly: "Establish a Picklist Upper Bound Limit — you can enforce an upper bound limit of inactive values on existing picklists", and explains why: "enforcing limits on inactive values for unrestricted picklists can improve performance and improve your Salesforce org's overall health." New unrestricted picklists already carry a default limit of 4,000 inactive values; the setting extends that ceiling to the older fields where the values have piled up, and the same page offers bulk deletion of the inactive values that already exist.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Global Values in Picklist Value Sets) — a global value set shares one list across fields; it does nothing about the inactive values already accumulated on these fields, and global value sets have their own combined active-plus-inactive limit of 1,000.
Option C (Remove the upper bound on inactive picklist values) — removing the limit is the opposite of the fix; Salesforce warns that "if your org's inactive unrestricted picklist values go unchecked, performance degrades."
Option D (Convert the picklist fields to a different field type) — converting to text throws away the controlled value list the business relies on, and does not clean up anything.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_manage_inactive_picklist_values.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=release-notes.rn_forcecom_fields_inactive_picklists.htm&language=en_US&release=230&type=5

corrected.note: The dump keyed Global Value Sets. Manage Inactive Picklist Values documents the fix as "Establish a Picklist Upper Bound Limit: you can enforce an upper bound limit of inactive values on existing picklists" in Picklist Settings; global value sets carry their own combined active-and-inactive limit of 1,000 and do not address the accumulated inactive values.

question: Ursa Major Solar (UMS) uses Cases to track customer complaints, an Issue__c object to represent known problems with its solar panels, and a Case_Issue__c junction object to relate known problems to customer complaints. Periodically, UMS conducts audits which require the auditing users to view Case_Issue__c records. Which access levels must be configured to allow UMS users to access Case_Issue__c records?
optionA: Read-Only access on Case and Issue__c
optionB: Read-Only access on Case and Case_Issue__c
optionC: Read-Only access on Case_Issue__c
optionD: Read-Only access on Issue__c and Case_Issue__c
explanation:
Read-Only access on Case and Issue__c, the two masters, is what unlocks the junction records. Custom Object Security: to view a detail record a user needs "Read permission and read access to the related master record. If the record has two master records in a many-to-many relationship, the user must have read access to both master records." The junction object's own sharing is derived, not configured separately.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Case and Case_Issue__c) — leaves out Issue__c, one of the two masters whose access is required.
Option C (Case_Issue__c only) — access to a junction record is decided by its masters; granting it on the junction alone does nothing.
Option D (Issue__c and Case_Issue__c) — leaves out Case, the other master.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.dev_security.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.relationships_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Ursa Major Solar wants to automate a welcome email to new clients and include a customized survey about their buying experience. An app builder is tasked with this project and has very little time to build the solution from scratch, but still needs to be able to fully customize the solution. What should the app builder do to meet the deadline and custom requirements?
optionA: Work with a developer to create custom Apex code and a Lightning web component survey to meet the criteria
optionB: Use Salesforce flow to build the survey declaratively to meet the criteria and send it to the customer as an email.
optionC: Choose a managed package from AppExchange that closely meets the requirements of the project, restricts programmatic development, but allows declarative development.
optionD: Choose an unmanaged package from AppExchange that closely meets the requirements of the project and allows programmatic development.
explanation:
An unmanaged package from AppExchange that closely fits the requirement gives the app builder a working starting point on day one and, because unmanaged components are installed as ordinary editable metadata, leaves everything open to programmatic and declarative customisation afterwards — which is what "fully customize" requires. Unmanaged packages are designed for distributing templates and open-source projects that installers are expected to modify.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Custom Apex and a Lightning web component) — building from scratch, which the time constraint rules out.
Option B (Build the survey declaratively in Flow and email it) — also building from scratch, and a flow is not a survey tool; Salesforce Surveys is the product for surveys.
Option C (A managed package that restricts programmatic development) — managed package components cannot be modified by the installing org, so it fails the "fully customize" requirement.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.pkg1_dev.meta/pkg1_dev/packaging_developing_unmanaged.htm
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.distribution_installing_packages.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: The dump keyed building the survey in Flow. The stem sets two constraints — very little time, so the solution cannot be built from scratch, and full customisation afterwards. An unmanaged AppExchange package meets both: its components install as editable metadata the org can change freely, whereas a managed package restricts what the subscriber may modify and a from-scratch flow build is what the deadline rules out. This is a judgment on the option set; no vendor page settles the scenario.

question: Northern Trail Outfitters (NTO) has created the custom objects Trail and Park in Salesforce to track trails and parks respectively. NTO wants to track the total number of trails a park has on the park record without writing any code. Which two actions should an app builder take to accomplish this requirement? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Use a formula field on the Park record to show the total number of trails.
optionB: Use a roll-up summary field on the Park record to show the total number of trails.
optionC: Use a master-detail relationship between the Park and Trail objects.
optionD: Use a lookup relationship between the Park and Trail objects.
explanation:
A roll-up summary field on Park, counting related Trail records, is the no-code way to hold a total on the parent — and a roll-up requires a master-detail relationship between the two objects: "The detail record must be related to the master through a master-detail relationship." So the two actions are to make Park the master of Trail (option C) and add a COUNT roll-up summary on Park (option B).
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Formula field on Park) — a formula field cannot aggregate child records; cross-object formulas only read fields from a parent record.
Option D (Lookup relationship between Park and Trail) — lookups "don't support sharing or roll-up summary fields", so a lookup would rule out the roll-up.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_roll_up_summary_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.overview_of_custom_object_relationships.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: DreamHouse Realty is building a custom Lightning app to track its expanding solar water collection business. The Lightning app currently contains a Custom Lightning record page with standard components. From which two resources should an app builder get custom components to bring into the new Lightning app? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Import Wizard
optionC: Apex Code
explanation:
Custom components come from two places: AppExchange, where packaged components are installed into the org, and Lightning components built by the org's own developers, which appear in the Custom section of the Lightning App Builder palette once deployed.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Import Wizard) — loads data records; it has nothing to do with components.
Option C (Apex code) — Apex is server-side logic; a Lightning page needs a Lightning web component or Aura component, which may call Apex but is not Apex.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.distribution_installing_packages.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/use-setup.html

question: Cloud Kicks recently implemented the application lifecycle management process to its release management strategy. Which category handles bug fixes and simple changes?
optionA: Roll
optionC: Minor
explanation:
Patch is the release category for bug fixes and small changes. In Salesforce's release-management vocabulary, patch releases carry bug fixes and simple changes, minor releases carry changes of limited impact that still need some testing, and major releases carry significant changes with dependencies and a full test cycle. The Trailhead package-update guidance uses the same scale: patches "are the smallest kind of updates — they fix bugs and make minor adjustments." This is methodology rather than a platform rule, so the references are orienting rather than decisive.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Roll) — not a release category.
Option B (Major) — significant changes with dependencies and a full regression cycle.
Option C (Minor) — limited-impact enhancements, such as a new trigger or a changed workflow, not simple bug fixes.
References:
https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/appexchange_app_updates/appexchange_app_updates_decide
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.changesets_best_practices.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A new app builder on the Cloud Kicks team is getting familiar with the data model. They want to see how standard objects and custom objects relate. Which functionality should the app builder use to view these relationships?
optionA: Object Manager
optionC: Schema Builder
explanation:
Schema Builder is the tool for seeing how objects relate: it "provides a dynamic environment for viewing and modifying all the objects and relationships in your app" and "provides details like the field values, required fields, and how objects are related by displaying lookup and master-detail relationships. You can view the fields and relationships for both standard and custom objects."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Object Manager) — shows one object at a time; it does not draw the relationships between objects.
Option B (Fields & Relationships) — the per-object field list inside Object Manager; it lists relationship fields for one object only.
Option D (Lightning App Builder) — builds pages, not the data model.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.schema_builder.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) has a time-sensitive need for a custom component to be built in 4 weeks. UC developers require additional enablement to complete the work and are backlogged by several months. Which option should an app builder suggest to meet this requirement?
optionA: Build a screen flow page.
optionC: Build a Lightning record page.
explanation:
An AppExchange solution is the answer when the deadline is fixed and the developers are not available: a packaged component is installed in minutes rather than built over months, and installing a package needs no developer at all.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Build a screen flow page) — a screen flow is not a custom component, and the requirement is the component itself.
Option C (Build a Lightning record page) — a page assembles components; it does not create the missing one.
Option D (Use a Bolt solution) — Lightning Bolt solutions are Experience Cloud site templates, not individual components.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.distribution_installing_packages.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: At Ursa Major Solar, there is a single Lightning record page for the Celestial Bodies custom object; however, there is a Lightning component the app builder wants to restrict to mobile app users. Which feature in the Lightning App Builder should be utilized?
optionA: Form factor checkboxes
optionC: Related list quick links
explanation:
A component visibility filter with the Device context restricts a component to one form factor. Visibility Rules on Lightning Pages, under Component Visibility Based on Form Factor: "With a filter using the Device context, you can set a component to display exclusively when its page is viewed in a specific experience, such as a phone or a desktop." It is set in the component's properties on the single record page, so no second page is needed.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Form factor checkboxes) — no such control exists in the Lightning App Builder; form factor is chosen when a page is activated, and per-component behaviour comes from visibility filters.
Option B (Highlights panel) — a component that shows key fields; it cannot hide another component by device.
Option C (Related list quick links) — another component, unrelated to device targeting.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.lightning_page_components_visibility.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: The dump keyed "form factor checkboxes", which is not a Lightning App Builder feature. Visibility Rules on Lightning Pages documents the mechanism: "With a filter using the Device context, you can set a component to display exclusively when its page is viewed in a specific experience, such as a phone or a desktop" — a component visibility filter.

question: Universal Containers has the Account object's Organization-Wide Default set to Private. The marketing team owns Accounts; however, they also need to be able to see the sales team's Accounts. Both the sales and marketing teams are in completely different branches of the role hierarchy. Which feature should be used to enable marketing to see sales-owned accounts?
optionA: Sharing rules
optionC: Aliases
explanation:
Sharing rules are the feature for opening one team's records to another team when the role hierarchy cannot do it. An owner-based sharing rule shares records "by who owns them" — records owned by users in the sales role or group — with the marketing public group, and it does so laterally across branches of the hierarchy that would otherwise never see each other's private accounts.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Public groups) — a group is a container of users; on its own it grants nothing. It is the target of a sharing rule, not the mechanism.
Option C (Aliases) — a user's short display name; unrelated to record access.
Option D (Assignment rules) — route new leads and cases to owners or queues; they do not share existing accounts.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_sharing_rules_owner.htm&type=5&language=en_US
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_controlling_access_using_hierarchies.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers has a single Contact Lightning record page. A component takes up a lot of room on the page and is NOT needed by users with a Marketing profile. What should the app builder use to solve this issue?
optionA: Component visibility filter
optionC: Detail page layouts
explanation:
A component visibility filter on the User context hides the component for the Marketing profile while keeping a single Contact record page. Visibility Rules on Lightning Pages: filters can use "fields from a global object like User", and "when you define one or more filters and set the filter logic for a component, it's hidden until the filter logic criteria are met" — so a filter such as User > Profile > Name not equal to Marketing does it.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (AppExchange) — a marketplace; it does not control what a profile sees on an existing page.
Option C (Detail page layouts) — page layouts govern fields and related lists, not Lightning page components, and would mean maintaining a second layout.
Option D (Field-level security) — hides fields, not components.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.lightning_page_components_visibility.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Ursa Major Solar has a lookup relationship between a custom Galaxy__c object and a custom Star__c object. An app builder wants to create a roll-up summary field that counts the total number of Star__c records related to each Galaxy__c record. How would the current configuration impact the ability to achieve the desired result?
optionA: The roll-up summary can be achieved by creating a formula field on the Galaxy__c object.
optionB: The lookup relationship will need to be converted to a master-detail relationship before a roll-up summary field can be created.
optionC: The roll-up summary can be achieved by creating a formula field on the Star__c object.
optionD: A roll-up summary field will need to be created on the Galaxy__c object with a field filter that reflects all related Star__c records.
explanation:
The lookup relationship must be converted to a master-detail relationship before a roll-up summary field can be created. Roll-Up Summary Field states that "the detail record must be related to the master through a master-detail relationship", and Considerations for Object Relationships allows the conversion "if the lookup field in all the records contains a value."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Formula field on Galaxy__c) — a formula field cannot count child records; cross-object formulas read parent fields only.
Option C (Formula field on Star__c) — a formula on the child cannot produce a count on the parent.
Option D (Roll-up summary on Galaxy__c with a filter) — the roll-up cannot be created at all while the relationship is a lookup, whatever filter it carries.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_roll_up_summary_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.relationships_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: At AW Computing, the Candidate object has a checkbox field for Previous Experience and a number field for Years of Previous Experience. The recruiting team wants the number field to display only if the Previous Experience field is checked. Which functionality should the app builder use to meet this requirement?
optionA: Create two different page layouts and a process to change the layout if Previous Experience is checked.
optionB: Create a dependency between the Previous Experience and Years of Previous Experience fields.
optionC: Use Dynamic Forms to display the Years of Previous Experience field if Previous Experience is checked.
optionD: Use a Visualforce component on the candidate page layout to conditionally display the fields.
explanation:
Dynamic Forms with a visibility rule on the Years of Previous Experience field is the built-in way to show one field only when another is set. Visibility Rules on Lightning Pages: "you can make your Lightning record pages even more dynamic by setting visibility filters on Field and Field Section components" — here a filter of Previous Experience equals true.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Two page layouts and a process to switch them) — page layouts are assigned by profile and record type, not swapped by a process on a checkbox, and it would need two layouts to maintain for one field.
Option B (A field dependency) — dependencies control which picklist values are available, and a checkbox can control only a picklist; a number field cannot be dependent.
Option D (A Visualforce component) — custom code for something the Lightning App Builder does declaratively.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.dynamic_forms_overview.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.lightning_page_components_visibility.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: The dump keyed A and C on a question that asks for one functionality. Dynamic Forms alone meets it: a visibility rule on the Years of Previous Experience field shows it only when the checkbox is true. Two page layouts switched by a process would need a record-type change to swap layouts and is not how conditional display is built.

question: A new field is being created on a custom object. However, the app builder does not want the field to show up on pre-existing custom report types. What should the app builder do on the custom field setup to fulfill this requirement?
optionA: Remove the new field from all page layouts.
optionB: Remove visibility to all report profiles.
optionC: Grant read-only access to all report profiles.
optionD: Deselect auto add to custom report type.
explanation:
Deselecting Auto add to custom report type on the field is what keeps it off the existing custom report types. Auto Add is a per-field setting: "With Auto Add, custom fields that you add to a Salesforce object are added automatically to all the custom report types based on that object." Clearing it on this field means the pre-existing report types are left as they are.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Remove the field from all page layouts) — page layouts control record pages, not which fields a report type offers.
Option B (Remove visibility for all report profiles) — field-level security hides the field from users; it does not keep the field out of the report type definition and would hide it from users who should see it on records.
Option C (Grant read-only access to all report profiles) — a permission setting; it has no effect on report type membership.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=release-notes.rn_rd_reports_auto_add_custom_fields.htm&language=en_US&release=232&type=5

question: The Director of Customer Service wants to receive a notification when a case stays in the New status for more than four business hours. Which two automation processes should be used to accomplish this? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Validation Rule
optionC: Scheduled Apex
explanation:
Two automations can wait four business hours and then notify: a case escalation rule and a record-triggered flow with a scheduled path. Escalation rules are time-based by design — "the Age Over field is required, because escalation rules are time-based" — they honour business hours, and their actions include "Notify This User". A scheduled path lets a flow "run part of a flow at a dynamically scheduled time after a triggering event", so the notification can fire hours after the case entered the New status.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Validation rule) — runs at save and can only accept or reject the record; it cannot wait or notify.
Option C (Scheduled Apex) — could be coded, but the stem asks for automation processes an app builder configures, and both declarative tools cover it.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.rules_escalation_actions.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_concepts_trigger_scheduled_path.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks has a custom object with a private sharing setting. The business wants to share individual records with specific people or departments on a case-by-case basis. Which three options does the business user have to manually share individual records? Choose 3 answers.
optionA: Permission Set Groups
optionC: Users
explanation:
Manual sharing in Lightning Experience offers Users, Public Groups and Roles and Subordinates (options C, D and E). Grant Access to Records with Manual Sharing lists the search-dropdown types: Managers Groups, Manager Subordinates Groups, Public Groups, Users, Roles, Roles and Subordinates, Roles and Internal Subordinates, Roles, Internal and Portal Subordinates, and Territories. Note that the same page now marks Roles and Subordinates as "Deprecated. Use Roles and Internal Subordinates instead" — the option survives on the exam under its older name.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Permission Set Groups) — permission set groups bundle permissions; they are not a share target.
Option B (Private Groups) — not a Salesforce group type; the personal groups a user creates can be used for sharing, but "private groups" do not exist under that name.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.granting_access_to_records_lex.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An app builder at DreamHouse Realty created a custom object which has fields containing data from two different objects via related lookups. What is needed to create "with" or "without" reports on the new custom object?
optionA: Report Filters
optionC: Report Bucket Field
explanation:
A custom report type is what defines "with" or "without" relationships between objects. When adding a related object to a custom report type you choose whether "'A' records may or may not have related 'B' records", which produces the with-or-without style of report; a standard report type fixes the join.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Report filters) — filters narrow rows within a report type; they cannot add an object relationship.
Option B (Row-level formula) — computes a value per row; no object join.
Option C (Bucket field) — groups values in a column; no object join.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.reports_enhanced_defining_report_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Where can an app builder edit an existing app to add components to the utility bar?
optionA: Lightning App Builder
optionC: App Manager
explanation:
App Manager is where a Lightning app's utility bar is edited. Add a Utility Bar to Lightning Apps: "From the Home tab in Setup, enter App in the Quick Find box, then select App Manager. To edit or add a utility bar to an existing app, click Edit ... Click the Utility Items tab and add the utilities you want."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Lightning App Builder) — builds record, home and app pages; the utility bar is an app setting reached through App Manager.
Option B (Lightning Record Page) — a page type, not a place to configure an app.
Option D (App Menu) — orders the apps users see; it does not edit an app's contents.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.apps_lightning_utilities.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers is adding drone delivery to service offerings. The developer wrote and tested the code and the change set is ready to go. However, the deployment window will occur when the developer is on vacation. What can the app builder do to help ensure the code will successfully deploy to production?
optionA: Remove Apex classes from inbound change set.
optionC: Use a metadata package set.
explanation:
Validate the inbound change set in production ahead of the window. Change Sets Best Practices: "you can perform a test deployment of an inbound change set to view the success or failure messages that would occur with an actual deployment. This is a good idea if you are planning a deployment on a schedule ... To test deploy an inbound change set, click its name and then click Validate." A validation runs the Apex tests too, so failures surface while the developer is still available.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Remove the Apex classes) — the code is the point of the deployment.
Option B (Validate the outbound change set) — validation happens on the receiving org's inbound change set; the outbound side only uploads.
Option C (Use a metadata package set) — not a Salesforce feature.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.changesets_best_practices.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: When a sales rep submits an account for approval, Universal Containers wants the user to answer additional questions via a popup window to populate additional record fields. What should an app builder use to achieve the desired result?
optionA: Custom object
optionC: Custom button and Flow
explanation:
A custom button (quick action) that launches a screen flow gives the rep a popup of questions whose answers are written to the record before it is submitted. Start a Flow from a Quick Action: "users can run a screen flow with the click of a button on a Lightning record page. Create a quick action on an object and configure it to run an active screen flow. Then, add the quick action button to the Lightning record page layout."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Custom object) — stores data; it has no user interface of its own.
Option B (Visualforce page) — code where a screen flow does the job declaratively.
Option D (Custom Lightning component) — also code for a declarative need.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_actions.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: At Ursa Major Solar there is a requirement for a new field called Planet Details on the Planet object where users can write detailed descriptions that can include pictures and links. Which field type should the app builder use to fulfill this requirement?
optionA: URL
optionC: Long text area
explanation:
A Rich Text Area is the field type that carries pictures and links. Custom Field Types describes Text Area (Rich): "with the use of a toolbar, users can format the field content and add images and hyperlinks", with images of up to 1 MB in gif, jpeg or png.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (URL) — holds a single web address, not a description.
Option B (Multi-select picklist) — a list of predefined values; no free text, images or links.
Option C (Long text area) — up to 131,072 characters of plain text, but no formatting, images or hyperlinks.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.custom_field_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Sales managers want to be automatically notified any time there is a change to an Opportunity Close Date and want these changes to be tracked on the Opportunity. Which two configurations should an app builder recommend? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Enable Feed Tracking on Opportunities.
optionC: Activate Historical Trending for Opportunities.
optionD: Use a record-triggered flow on Opportunity and a Chatter post action.
explanation:
