Feed tracking on Opportunity records every Close Date change in the record's feed, which tracks the change and reaches anyone following the opportunity (option A). A record-triggered flow with a Post to Chatter action, triggered when Close Date changes, posts to (or mentions) the sales managers so they are actively notified (option D). Post to Chatter is one of the provided flow core actions.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (An outbound message) — sends a SOAP message to an external endpoint; it neither notifies a manager in Salesforce nor tracks the change on the record.
Option C (Historical Trending) — snapshots data for trend reports; it does not notify anyone.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.collab_feed_tracking.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_ref_elements_actions_list.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An app builder needs a custom solution and is considering using either AppExchange or their local developer community. The app builder wants to minimize the need for manual maintenance. What should the app builder consider?
optionA: An open-source unmanaged package
optionC: An open-source custom development
explanation:
A managed package from AppExchange minimises manual maintenance: the publisher upgrades it centrally, upgrades are pushed or installed without reworking customisations, and its components are protected from accidental edits. Unmanaged packages cannot be upgraded — a new version means uninstalling and reinstalling — and custom development is maintained entirely by the org.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (An open-source unmanaged package) — no upgrade path; every fix is manual.
Option B (An unmanaged package from AppExchange) — the same limitation regardless of where it comes from.
Option C (Open-source custom development) — the org owns every change and every fix.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.distribution_installing_packages.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.pkg1_dev.meta/pkg1_dev/packaging_developing_unmanaged.htm

question: Duplicate management for Leads has been implemented at Universal Containers, but it seems duplicate leads are still being created. The Org-Wide Default (OWD) is set to Private for Leads. Which two actions help prevent duplicate Leads from being created? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Change the Lead Duplicate Rule details to Bypass Sharing Rules.
optionB: Change the Lead Assignment Rule to check for duplicates.
optionC: Change OWD for Leads to Public Read Only.
optionD: Change the Lead Duplicate actions to Block on Create.
explanation:
Two settings on the lead duplicate rule close the gaps. With a Private org-wide default, a rule that enforces sharing rules only compares a new lead against leads the user can see, so duplicates owned by other users slip through — switching the rule's record-level security to Bypass sharing rules makes it compare against every lead (option A). And if the Action on Create is Allow (alert only), users can click through the warning; setting it to Block stops the duplicate from being saved (option D). Customize Duplicate Rules describes both the record-level security settings and the Block option, and advises arranging rules "so that rules with the Block option run before rules with the Allow option."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Make the lead assignment rule check for duplicates) — assignment rules route leads to owners or queues; they cannot detect duplicates.
Option C (Change the OWD for Leads to Public Read Only) — would widen visibility for everyone just to make the rule see more records; the rule's own Bypass sharing rules setting does that without changing security.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.duplicate_rules_create.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers has a custom picklist called Support Level on the Account object. They would like to see the real-time value of Support Level on all Case records. How should an app builder implement this requirement?
optionA: Create a formula field on the Account object using the ISPICKVAL function.
optionB: Create a Lookup Relationship on the Case object.
optionC: Create a roll-up summary field using Support Level on the Account object.
optionD: Create a formula field on the Case object using the TEXT function.
explanation:
A formula field on Case using TEXT(Account.Support_Level__c) shows the Account's picklist value in real time. A cross-object formula "can reference merge fields from a master ('parent') object" and "also works with lookup relationships", so a Case can read its parent Account; TEXT() is what turns a picklist into displayable text, and because the value is computed on read it is always current.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Formula on Account using ISPICKVAL) — ISPICKVAL returns true or false, and a field on Account does not appear on Case records.
Option B (Lookup relationship on Case) — Case already looks up to Account; a new lookup does not surface a field value.
Option C (Roll-up summary on Account) — roll-ups aggregate child records on the parent; this requirement flows the other way, parent to child.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.customize_cross_object.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A business user wants a quick way to edit a record's status and enter a custom due date field from the record's feed in the Salesforce mobile app. What should be used to accomplish this?
optionA: Custom quick access link
optionC: Custom button
explanation:
A custom object-specific action of type Update a Record is built for this: "Object-specific Update a Record actions make it easy for users to edit records. You can define the fields that are available for update." The action appears in the record's action bar and feed in the Salesforce mobile app, showing only the status and due date fields.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Custom quick access link) — not a Salesforce feature.
Option C (Custom button) — custom buttons open URLs or run JavaScript in Classic; they do not present an edit form from the mobile feed.
Option D (Custom URL formula field) — a field that renders a link, not an edit form.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.actions_overview_object_specific.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An app builder wants to create a new field using Schema Builder. Who will get access to the new field by default?
optionA: No profiles
optionC: Internal profiles
explanation:
Internal profiles get the new field by default. Create Fields with Schema Builder: "By default, the field level security for custom fields is set to visible and editable for internal profiles. Fields that aren't normally editable, such as formulas and roll-up summary fields, are visible and read-only." Schema Builder Considerations adds the definition — internal profiles are "those not cloned from Partner User or Customer Portal Manager."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (No profiles) — the default is visible and editable, not hidden.
Option B (All profiles) — partner and customer portal profiles are excluded from the default.
Option D (Standard profiles) — the default is by internal versus external, not standard versus custom.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.schema_builder_elements_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.schema_builder_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers uses a custom object called Projects. When managers assign projects, they set a custom field on the Project record called Estimated Hours. Once set, users should be able to decrease but not increase the value. How can an app builder meet this requirement?
optionA: Create a validation rule that uses the ISCHANGED function.
optionB: Create a formula default value for the custom field.
optionC: Create a validation rule that uses the PRIORVALUE function.
optionD: Create a formula field that uses the PREVGROUPVAL function.
explanation:
A validation rule using PRIORVALUE compares the new value with the old one and rejects an increase: Estimated_Hours__c > PRIORVALUE(Estimated_Hours__c). PRIORVALUE "returns the previous value of a field" and is available in validation rules; "when users create a record, this function returns the value of the field referenced rather than null", so the rule does not fire on creation.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (A validation rule with ISCHANGED) — ISCHANGED only reports that the value changed; it cannot tell an increase from a decrease.
Option B (A formula default value) — sets an initial value; it cannot police later edits.
Option D (A formula field with PREVGROUPVAL) — PREVGROUPVAL is a report summary function, not a field-level check.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.customize_functions_priorvalue.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.customize_functions_ischanged.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A custom field on an Account is used to track finance information about a customer. Only members of the finance team have access to this field. However, the business wants to allow one customer service agent, who is assigned the Customer Service profile, read-only access to this field for special circumstances. What is the recommended solution to grant the customer service agent access to the field?
optionA: Create a new profile to allow for read-only access to the field via field level security and assign it to the agent.
optionB: Create a permission set that allows read-only access to the field via field level security and assign it to the agent.
optionC: Update the custom field's field-level security in Setup to allow the agent read-only access to the field.
optionD: Update the Customer Service Profile already assigned to the agent to allow for read-only access to the field via field level security.
explanation:
A permission set granting read access to the field, assigned to that one agent, is the recommended solution: permission sets extend access for individual users without touching the profile everyone else shares. Field-level security can be set on a permission set exactly as on a profile.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (A new profile for the agent) — profiles are meant to be few; cloning one for a single exception multiplies maintenance.
Option C (Edit the field's field-level security in Setup for the agent) — field-level security is set per profile or permission set, never per user, so this cannot be done for one person without changing a profile.
Option D (Update the Customer Service profile) — grants the field to every user on that profile, not just the one agent.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.perm_sets_overview.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.users_profiles_field_perms.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers wants customers to be able to open cases from a public-facing website. What should the app builder use to enable visitors to the website?
optionA: Web-to-case
optionC: Screen flow
explanation:
Web-to-Case generates an HTML form for a public website whose submissions create cases in Salesforce, which is exactly what website visitors need.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Outbound message) — sends data out of Salesforce to an endpoint; it does not accept submissions from a website.
Option C (Screen flow) — runs for authenticated users or on an Experience Cloud site; a public web page needs Web-to-Case's form.
Option D (Email-to-Case) — creates cases from inbound email, not from a website form.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.setting_up_web-to-case.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An app builder installed a custom Lightning component from AppExchange. What should be done next in order to configure the component for use in a record page?
optionA: Edit a record page using the Page Layout editor > Drag the Visualforce component onto the page.
optionB: Edit a record page using Lightning App Builder > Drag the component onto the page.
optionC: Edit a record page using App Manager > Drag the component onto the page.
optionD: Edit a record page using the Page Layout editor > Drag the component onto the page.
explanation:
An installed custom Lightning component is placed on a record page in the Lightning App Builder: edit the page and drag the component from the Custom or Custom - Managed section of the palette onto the canvas. The builder handles standard, custom and AppExchange components alike — "this behavior applies to standard components, custom components, and components from AppExchange."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Page Layout editor and a Visualforce component) — the page layout editor places Visualforce pages, not Lightning components, and the installed component is not Visualforce.
Option C (App Manager) — configures apps and utility bars, not record pages.
Option D (Page Layout editor) — Lightning components are not available in the page layout editor.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.lightning_page_components_visibility.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.lightning_page_components.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: DreamHouse Realty wants to make sure an Opportunity has a field, Expected_Close_Date__c, populated before it is allowed to enter the Qualified stage. How should an app builder solution this request?
optionA: Page Layout
optionC: Activity History
explanation:
A validation rule enforces it: AND(ISPICKVAL(StageName, "Qualified"), ISBLANK(Expected_Close_Date__c)) blocks the save with a message. Considerations and Guidelines for Creating Paths confirms this is the tool even when a Path is in use — "you can't use the page layout to require different fields in different steps. However, you can set up validation rules based on a path step."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Page layout) — a layout's required fields apply at every stage, so the field would be mandatory from creation, not only at Qualified.
Option C (Activity history) — a related list of past activities; unrelated.
Option D (Record type) — record types choose layouts and picklist values; they cannot make a field conditionally required.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_validation_rules_tips.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.path_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers uses a custom object called Reviews to capture information generated by interviewers during the candidate process. The Review records are visible to any user that has access to the related custom Candidate record. The VP of Human Resources wants the comment field on the Review to be private to anyone outside of the HR department. How should the app builder meet this requirement?
optionA: Create a page layout with the field and use field-level security to hide the field from all other users.
optionB: Create a sharing rule to share the field with the VP of HR with Role and Subordinates.
optionC: Create a page layout with the field for HR users and another page layout without the field for all other users.
optionD: Create an Apex sharing rule to share the field with users that have "HR" in their role.
explanation:
Field-level security is the only control that hides a field from users who can otherwise see the record: put the comment field on the layout and make it visible to HR profiles or permission sets only. Sharing decides who sees the Review record; field permissions decide which fields on it they can see.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (A sharing rule for the VP's role and subordinates) — sharing rules share whole records; they cannot restrict a single field.
Option C (Two page layouts, one without the field) — layouts are cosmetic; a field left off a layout is still visible in reports, list views and the API, so it is not private.
Option D (An Apex sharing rule) — Apex managed sharing also operates on records, not fields, and "HR in their role" is not how field access is granted.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.users_profiles_field_perms.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: After discovering a second sun in the solar system, Ursa Major Solar wants to change the field relationship between Sun__c and Planet__c to a lookup rather than a master-detail. What should an app builder consider about the effect on reporting before making this change?
optionA: Existing reports created under the Sun__c with Planet__c report type made by Salesforce will be unusable, but not deleted.
optionB: Existing roll-up summary fields will be deleted from the Sun__c object and from any reports where they were added.
optionC: Existing roll-up summary fields will remain on the Sun__c object and available for reporting, but will no longer update.
optionD: Existing reports created under the Sun__c with Planet__c report type made by Salesforce will be deleted.
explanation:
Reports built on the standard "Sun__c with Planet__c" report type become unusable, not deleted. Considerations for Object Relationships warns that "converting a relationship from lookup to master-detail or vice versa can cause existing custom reports to become unusable due to the different standard report types available for each type of relationship", and adds that "if you revert your relationship back to the original type, the reports are restored and become usable again" — which is only possible because they were never deleted.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Roll-up summary fields will be deleted) — the conversion is blocked while roll-ups exist: "you can convert a master-detail relationship to a lookup relationship as long as no roll-up summary fields exist on the master object", so the fields have to be removed first, not deleted by the change.
Option C (Roll-ups remain but stop updating) — same reason; roll-up summary fields cannot survive the conversion at all.
Option D (Reports will be deleted) — they become unusable and are restored if the relationship is reverted.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.relationships_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.notes_on_changing_custom_field_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers deployed an app in a large change set from a Developer sandbox to a Developer Pro sandbox used for testing. After testing, changes had to be made to several of the components in the change set. How should an app builder move the new changes to the Developer Pro sandbox?
optionA: Rename the change set, add the changes and re-deploy.
optionB: Clone the change set and re-deploy.
optionC: Refresh the test sandbox and re-deploy the change set.
optionD: Update the change set and re-deploy.
explanation:
Clone the change set, add the changed components and deploy again. An uploaded change set is frozen — Change Sets Best Practices: "After you upload a change set, you can't change its contents. If you need to add dependent components to a change set you already uploaded, clone the change set, add the dependent components, and then upload it again."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Rename the change set and add the changes) — its contents cannot be edited after upload, whatever it is called.
Option C (Refresh the test sandbox and redeploy) — refreshing wipes the sandbox and does not put the new component versions into the change set.
Option D (Update the change set and redeploy) — not possible once uploaded.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.changesets_best_practices.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Ursa Major Solar wants to create a relationship between the standard Contact object and a custom Solar Project object. Contacts can potentially be related to multiple Solar Project objects, and a Solar Project can have multiple Contacts associated with it. How should an app builder configure the data model?
optionA: Two Master-detail relationships on a new custom object
optionB: One Master-detail relationship on Contact and one Master-detail relationship on Solar Project
optionC: Two Lookup relationships on a new custom object
optionD: One Lookup relationship on Contact and one Lookup relationship on Solar Project
explanation:
Two master-detail relationships on a new custom object is the many-to-many pattern. Object Relationships Overview: "You can use master-detail relationships to model many-to-many relationships between any two objects ... when modeling a many-to-many relationship, you use a junction object to connect the two objects you want to relate to each other." The junction object (for example Project Contact) holds one master-detail field to Contact and one to Solar Project, so a contact can sit on many projects and a project can have many contacts.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (One master-detail on Contact and one on Solar Project) — a master-detail field lives on the detail side and gives each record a single master; putting one on each object does not express many-to-many, and a standard object such as Contact cannot be made the detail of a custom object.
Option C (Two lookup relationships on a new custom object) — this also links the records, but lookups "don't support sharing or roll-up summary fields"; the documented junction-object pattern uses master-detail, which gives inherited sharing and cascade delete.
Option D (One lookup on each object) — each record could point at only one record on the other side, which is one-to-one, not many-to-many.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.overview_of_custom_object_relationships.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.relationships_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: The dump keyed one master-detail relationship on each object. A many-to-many relationship is modelled with a junction object carrying two master-detail relationships, one to each master — "you create a custom object ... a junction object to connect the two objects you want to relate to each other" — and neither Contact nor Solar Project can hold a master-detail field pointing at the other.

question: Universal Containers has deployed custom tabs to production via change sets, without including the profile settings or permission sets. What is the setting for the visibility of custom tabs?
optionA: Custom tabs are hidden for all users.
optionB: Custom tabs are default off for all users.
optionC: Custom tabs are default on for all users.
explanation:
Deployed custom tabs are hidden for everyone until profile settings arrive. Components Available in Change Sets: "Deployed custom tabs are hidden by default for all users. They're visible only if the change set also contains profiles that set the visibility property appropriately. Professional Edition orgs are an exception. Deployed custom tabs in those orgs are always visible by default."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Default Off for all users) — Default Off still lets users add the tab themselves; the documented state is hidden.
Option C (Default On) — only in Professional Edition, which the stem does not describe.
Option D (Custom tabs are not deployed) — the tab deploys; its visibility is what is missing.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.changesets_about_components.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An app builder wants to create a custom object and 10 fields. What should they use to create the object, fields, and relationships quickly from one place?
optionA: Schema Builder
optionC: Manage Field Permissions
explanation:
Schema Builder creates objects, fields and relationships from one canvas: "you can view your existing schema and interactively add new custom objects, custom fields, and relationships, simply by dragging and dropping", which "eliminates the need to click from page to page." Remember its one gap — a field added there "isn't automatically added to the object's page layout."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Lightning Object Creator) — builds a single object from a spreadsheet; it is not the place to draw relationships between objects.
Option C (Manage Field Permissions) — the field-level security dialog; it edits access, not the schema.
Option D (Developer Console) — a coding tool; objects and fields are not created there.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.schema_builder.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.schema_builder_elements_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An app builder wants to update a field on the parent record when a child record connected via lookup is deleted. Which automation should the app builder use?
optionA: Record-triggered flow
optionC: Autolaunched flow
explanation:
A record-triggered flow on the child object, configured to run when a record is deleted, can look up the parent through the lookup field and update it. Getting Started with Record-Triggered Flows: "Record-triggered flows automatically run when someone creates, updates, or deletes a record in Salesforce", and updating a related record needs the after-save context that a delete trigger provides.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Validation rule) — validation rules do not run on delete and cannot update another record.
Option C (Autolaunched flow) — runs only when something invokes it; it has no delete trigger of its own.
Option D (Quick action) — a user-initiated action, not an automatic response to a deletion.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.automate_flow_build_get_started_record_triggered_flows.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_concepts_trigger_record.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The VP of Sales at AW Computing would like a Roll-Up Summary field on the Account object to aggregate the amount of opportunities related to an Account. The app builder is unable to implement this change. Why is the app builder unable to fulfill the request?
optionA: The default currency is not an active currency in the organization.
optionB: The organization has Advanced Currency Management enabled.
optionC: Roll-Up Summary fields are unavailable on the Account object.
optionD: Currency fields are unable to be referenced in Roll-Up Summary fields.
explanation:
Advanced Currency Management is the blocker. About Advanced Currency Management: "if you enable advanced currency management, you can't create roll-up summary fields that calculate currency on the opportunity object rolling up to the account object. You also can't filter on the opportunity currency field on the account object." Existing currency roll-ups from opportunities to accounts are disabled when the feature is turned on.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Default currency is not active) — currency activation affects which currencies records can use, not whether roll-ups can be defined.
Option C (Roll-up summary fields are unavailable on Account) — Roll-Up Summary Field lists "Accounts using the values of related opportunities" as a supported case.
Option D (Currency fields can't be referenced) — currency is one of the field types a SUM roll-up accepts; the restriction is specific to advanced currency management.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.administration_about_advanced_currency_management.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_roll_up_summary_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks wants to display 12 key fields at once in a separate section at the top of opportunity records on the desktop. Which component should an app builder add to the record page to enable this functionality?
optionA: Custom Lightning Web Component
optionC: Path
explanation:
The Highlights Panel is the component that shows key fields in a band at the top of the record. The Dynamic Highlights Panel "displays up to 12 key record fields, which are configured in Lightning App Builder", and the classic highlights panel shows the fields from the object's compact layout.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Custom Lightning Web Component) — code for something a standard component already does.
Option C (Path) — shows stage progress with up to five key fields per stage, not a fixed set of record fields at the top.
Option D (Accordion) — collapsible sections that hold other components; not a field display.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.dynamic_highlights_panel.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.compact_layout_overview.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Northern Trail Outfitters wants to initiate a daily backup of its Salesforce org. Which tool should an app builder recommend for this task?
optionA: Refresh full copy sandbox
optionC: Data Export Service
explanation:
The Data Export Service, under Setup > Data Export, is Salesforce's built-in tool for scheduling exports of the org's data as zipped CSV files — the answer this item wants. Note the cadence the documentation actually offers: weekly exports in Enterprise, Performance and Unlimited editions and monthly in Professional and Developer, with the files kept for 48 hours. A genuinely daily backup is not something the native service schedules; that is where a backup product comes in.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Refresh a Full sandbox) — a sandbox is a copy for development and testing, refreshable at most every 29 days; it is not a backup.
Option B (An AppExchange package) — a backup product can run daily, but the item credits the platform's own export service.
Option D (Report export) — exports one report's rows; it is not an org backup.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.admin_exportdata.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: The Data Export Service is the platform backup tool the item credits, but it does not run daily: Export Backup Data from Salesforce offers weekly exports (Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited) or monthly exports (Professional, Developer). The item's "daily" wording overstates the native cadence; a true daily backup needs an AppExchange backup product or Salesforce Backup.

question: An app builder installs an unmanaged package in a full copy sandbox that is an exact match for production, and now they are ready to install it in production. The app builder attempts to install the package in production, and it fails. Why did the package fail to install?
optionA: Incorrect license types
optionC: Apex unit test failures
explanation:
Apex unit test failures are the likely cause. Installing a package that contains Apex runs tests — "when you install a component that contains Apex, the unit tests contained in the new package, and all unit tests for your org are run" — and in a production org failing tests or insufficient coverage stop the install, whereas a sandbox tolerates them. A full sandbox matching production's metadata does not guarantee the tests pass against production's data and coverage thresholds.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Incorrect license types) — the sandbox is a copy of production, so licensing is the same in both.
Option B (Object limits exceeded) — a full sandbox mirrors production's limits and metadata; if the objects fit in one they fit in the other.
Option D (Package features not compatible) — features enabled in production are copied to a full sandbox, so a feature mismatch is not the difference.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.distribution_installing_packages.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.changesets_best_practices.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers allows all employees to submit reviews for leadership using a custom object called Review. These Reviews should only be visible to the HR department and the employee who submitted the record. Which three steps should an app builder take to properly control access to Reviews? Choose 3 answers.
optionA: Add a Master-Detail(User) field on the Review object.
optionC: Remove Review Read permission from non-HR Department user Profiles.
optionE: Create a criteria-based Sharing Rule for the HR Department.
explanation:
Three settings together: set the org-wide default for Review to Private so only the submitting owner sees a record by default (option B); disable Grant Access Using Hierarchies on the object so the submitter's managers do not inherit access up the role tree (option D); and add a criteria-based sharing rule that shares all Reviews with the HR department's group (option E). Grant Access Using Hierarchies can be switched off only for custom objects, which Review is.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (A master-detail to User) — User cannot be the master of a master-detail relationship, and ownership already ties the record to its submitter.
Option C (Remove Read permission from non-HR profiles) — object permissions are all-or-nothing; taking away Read would stop employees seeing the reviews they submitted.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_sharing_owd_about.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_controlling_access_using_hierarchies.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.security_sharing_rules_criteria.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An app builder at Universal Containers has been asked to add the Chatter feed to a custom object record page. Which approach should the app builder use?
optionA: Add a custom Chatter feed component.
optionB: Add the standard related list component.
optionC: Add the standard Chatter feed component.
optionD: Add the Chatter feed component from the AppExchange.
explanation:
The standard Chatter component is the one to add: "Use it to place a publisher and feed combo on a record page." Feed tracking must be enabled on the custom object for the feed to appear — "in Lightning Experience, most objects don't show a Chatter tab unless feed tracking is enabled for the object."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (A custom Chatter feed component) — unnecessary; the standard component exists.
Option B (The standard related list component) — shows related records, not the feed.
Option D (A Chatter feed component from the AppExchange) — the feed is built in; no package is needed.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.lightning_page_components.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.collab_feed_tracking.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: DreamHouse Realty wants to import its property records from an external system into Salesforce. The app builder will use an external ID field to house the property ID from the external system. Which two details should the app builder know when using external ID fields?
optionA: Each org can have up to 25 custom external ID fields.
optionB: Each object can have up to 25 custom external ID fields.
optionC: An external ID field can be a URL field.
optionD: An external ID field can be an auto-number field.
explanation:
Two facts from Custom Field Attributes: "for each object that can have custom fields, you can set up to 25 custom auto-number, email, number, or text fields as external IDs." So the limit is per object (option B) and an auto-number field qualifies (option D).
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (25 per org) — the limit is per object, not per org.
Option C (A URL field) — URL is not one of the four permitted types: auto-number, email, number, text.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.custom_field_attributes.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks (CK) switched to Lightning Experience and started using Chatter across its global workforce to support its fast-paced sales cycle. CK loves Chatter but struggles with gathering feedback from core team members, including understanding who is available to respond. Which two ways could CK use Chatter to solve this problem? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Streams
optionC: Polls
explanation:
Streams and Out of Office answer the two halves. Chatter Streams "are custom feeds that you create by combining multiple related feeds into one feed ... from people, groups, and records", so the posts of the core team members can be followed in one place. Out of Office lets a user schedule a message that "appears next to your name", telling colleagues who is unavailable to respond. (The published dumps disagree between Streams and Polls for the first half; Streams is the feature that gathers a chosen set of people's posts, which is what the stem describes.)
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Topics) — tag posts by subject so they can be found; they do not gather a specific group's feed or show availability.
Option C (Polls) — a post type for collecting votes on a question; it does not show who is available and reaches whoever sees the post, not a chosen team.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=experience.collab_chatter_streams_overview.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=experience.collab_profile_out_of_office.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A business user at Universal Containers wants to update an Account directly from an Opportunity record. What should the app builder create to allow the business user to make these edits?
optionA: Opportunity fields updated by a process.
optionB: Formula fields displaying the Account fields.
optionC: An update record action with a related record component.
optionD: An update record action with a record detail component.
explanation:
An Update a Record quick action on Account, shown through the Related Record component on the Opportunity page, lets users edit the account without leaving the opportunity. Standard Lightning Page Components: the Related Record component displays "the details of a related record, including the details of a parent record" and "provides your users with built-in record creation, inline edit ... because the component uses actions. To use the component, an object must have an associated quick action to update the records."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Opportunity fields updated by a process) — automation writing to Opportunity, not a user editing the Account.
Option B (Formula fields showing Account fields) — read-only; formulas display parent values but cannot edit them.
Option D (An update action with a record detail component) — Record Detail shows the current record (the Opportunity), not its parent Account.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.lightning_page_components.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.actions_overview_object_specific.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A production org includes custom objects containing confidential information. A sandbox is needed that includes data records, excludes all of the confidential objects, and can be refreshed weekly. Which steps should an app builder take to meet these requirements?
optionA: Create a Developer Pro Sandbox and schedule Data Loader to download selected object data weekly.
optionB: Create a Full Copy Sandbox and use a sandbox template.
optionC: Create a Partial Copy Sandbox and use a sandbox template.
optionD: Create a Developer Sandbox and schedule Data Loader to download selected object data weekly.
explanation:
A Partial Copy sandbox with a sandbox template. Sandbox templates choose which objects' records are copied, so the confidential objects are simply left out of the template, and the Partial Copy type refreshes every 5 days, so a weekly refresh fits. Sandbox Licenses and Storage Limits by Type marks templates as required for Partial Copy sandboxes and gives the 5-day refresh interval.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Developer Pro plus scheduled Data Loader) — Developer Pro copies metadata only; loading data by hand every week is the manual process the sandbox type should avoid.
Option B (Full Copy with a template) — templates work on Full sandboxes too, but a Full sandbox refreshes only every 29 days, so weekly is impossible.
Option D (Developer plus scheduled Data Loader) — same objection as A, with only 200 MB of storage.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.data_sandbox_environments.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.data_sandbox_templates.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: DreamHouse Realty requires that field value changes for certain fields such as Asking_Price__c and Real_Estate_Agent__c on their House__c custom object show up prominently on Chatter. Which Chatter feature should the app builder use?
optionA: Topics
optionC: Pin Field
explanation:
Feed tracking is the Chatter feature that posts field changes to a record's feed. Customize Chatter Feed Tracking: "when you enable feed tracking for objects and records, users see updates for the objects and records that they follow", and "you can configure feed tracking for ... custom objects" and choose which fields are tracked — here Asking_Price__c and Real_Estate_Agent__c on House__c.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Topics) — categorise posts; they do not generate them from field changes.
Option C (Pin Field) — not a Chatter feature.
Option D (Publisher actions) — the actions users take from the publisher (Post, File, Poll); they do not track field changes.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.collab_feed_tracking.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) has a custom Invoice object and a custom Invoice Line Item object. The Invoice Line Item object has a lookup relationship to the Invoice. UC would like to convert the lookup relationship to a master-detail relationship but is unable to do so. Which two reasons could be preventing this relationship conversion? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: There are already two master-detail relationships on the Invoice Line Item.
optionB: Custom objects are unable to be on the detail side of a master-detail Relationship.
optionC: Invoice Line Item records exist without having the Invoice lookup field populated.
optionD: There is a roll-up summary field on the Invoice object.
explanation:
Two documented blockers fit. Considerations for Object Relationships: "you can convert a lookup relationship to a master-detail relationship if the lookup field in all the records contains a value" — so Invoice Line Items with an empty Invoice lookup prevent it (option C). And Object Relationships Overview caps a custom object at "up to two master-detail relationships", so an Invoice Line Item that already has two cannot take a third (option A).
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Custom objects can't be on the detail side) — custom objects are the usual detail objects; a custom Invoice Line Item can absolutely be a detail.
Option D (A roll-up summary on Invoice) — roll-ups block the reverse conversion (master-detail to lookup), and cannot exist across a lookup in the first place.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.relationships_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.overview_of_custom_object_relationships.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Ursa Major Solar is ramping up the sales team to meet increased demand. As part of the short ramp-up for these new reps, the manager wants to provide a help guide to enable reps to easily get help where needed during the different sales processes. Which solution should an app builder recommend?
optionA: Path
optionC: Journey Builder
explanation:
Path gives reps stage-by-stage guidance on the record itself: each step shows up to five key fields and "up to 1,000 characters of guidance for success", which is exactly a help guide that appears where reps are working in the sales process.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Chatter Publisher) — posts and files; not stage guidance.
Option C (Journey Builder) — a Marketing Cloud tool for customer journeys, not internal rep guidance.
Option D (Flow) — could build a wizard, but Path already provides in-context guidance declaratively on the opportunity page.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.path_overview.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.path_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The brokers at DreamHouse Realty (DR) are having an issue when using the Salesforce mobile app on their iPhones. There are several key fields on the Contact record they need access to at a glance. Because of the small screen, they currently have to scroll down the page to view the information. What should the app builder at DR use to configure the Salesforce mobile app to show these key fields at the top of the screen?
optionA: Compact layout
optionC: Object specific action
explanation:
A compact layout decides the fields shown at the top of a record in the mobile app: "a compact layout displays a record's key fields at a glance in the Salesforce mobile app", and "in the Salesforce mobile app, the fields that you assign to a compact layout appear in an object record's highlights area (shows up to ten fields)."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Record Detail component) — shows the full field list, which is what the brokers are scrolling through.
Option C (Object-specific action) — creates or updates records; it does not choose highlight fields.
Option D (Mobile navigation) — orders the navigation menu items, not fields on a record.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.compact_layout_overview.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks received a new requirement to calculate summaries from child objects of a standard object. The team would prefer to solve this declaratively. What are two considerations an app builder should evaluate? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: An app builder is unable to change a lookup to a master-detail relationship.
optionB: An object can have up to two master-detail relationships.
optionC: A trigger on save or update can kick off calculations.
optionD: A value is required in all records of the lookup field prior to converting to a master-detail relationship.
explanation:
Summaries from child objects, done declaratively, means roll-up summary fields, and those need a master-detail relationship. Two considerations follow. "Each custom object can have up to two master-detail relationships" (option B), and a lookup can become master-detail only "if the lookup field in all the records contains a value" (option D).
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Unable to change a lookup to master-detail) — the conversion is allowed once every record has a value in the lookup.
Option C (A trigger on save can kick off calculations) — true of Apex, but the team asked for a declarative solution, so it is not a consideration for roll-ups.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.overview_of_custom_object_relationships.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.relationships_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_roll_up_summary_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which three standard component types are available in the Lightning App Builder? Choose 3 answers.
optionA: Plain text
optionC: Filter list
explanation:
Rich Text, List View (called Filter List when this item was written) and Recent Items are all standard Lightning App Builder components. Standard Lightning Page Components documents each: Rich Text ("add text and simple HTML markup to your Lightning page"), List View ("points to a list view and displays the first few records from that view") and Recent Items ("displays a list of the most recently used items").
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Plain text) — no such component; text goes in the Rich Text component.
Option D (Report details) — no such component; the standard report component is Report Chart, which embeds a chart from a report.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.lightning_page_components.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: The dump keyed "Report details", which is not a Lightning App Builder component (the report component is Report Chart). Standard Lightning Page Components lists Rich Text, List View and Recent Items; the List View component was called Filter List in older releases, which is the name this item uses.

question: After a deal is closed, Cloud Kicks (CK) wants to assign a user as a customer service manager (CSM) in addition to the account owner, and would like a new field to easily track and report which CSM is assigned to the Account. Which solution should an app builder use for this request?
optionA: Multi-select picklist field
optionC: Lookup field
explanation:
A lookup relationship field to the User object is the right design: it stores a real user record that can be tracked, reported on and filtered. Object Relationships Overview uses exactly this shape as its example — "create a lookup relationship from the PTO Request custom object with the user object" — and lookups to User are the standard way to hold a second responsible person alongside the Owner field.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Multi-select picklist) — a hand-maintained list of names that goes stale as staff change and cannot be joined to the User record in reports.
Option B (Picklist) — same problem, and it allows only values an admin has typed in.
Option D (Text field) — free text invites typos and cannot be related to the actual user.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.overview_of_custom_object_relationships.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks has a shipment date on each shipment that is sent out. Dispatchers need more details on the day and time the shipment was sent out. The app builder needs to change the current field type that is used from Date to Date/Time. What should the app builder be aware of when it comes to data already in the system?
optionA: The change will be instant
optionB: Historical data will be updated to a 12:00 timestamp.
optionC: The field name will change.
explanation:
Data loss is the documented risk. Considerations for Converting the Field Type of a Custom Field opens with "to avoid losing data, only convert custom fields that have no data", and its list of conversions that "can cause data loss" begins with "changing to or from type Date or Date/Time." An app builder should export or back up the existing shipment dates before changing the type.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (The change will be instant) — a type change can require rewriting every record; the same page notes that "changing a custom field type can require changing many records at once" and that the conversion may be queued and completed later.
Option B (Historical data gets a 12:00 timestamp) — no Salesforce documentation describes a default time being written; the documented outcome is possible data loss.
Option C (The field name will change) — the API name and label are untouched by a type change.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.notes_on_changing_custom_field_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: The dump keyed "historical data will be updated to a 12:00 timestamp", a behaviour no Salesforce page documents. Considerations for Converting the Field Type of a Custom Field lists "changing to or from type Date or Date/Time" among the situations in which "changing the data type of an existing custom field can cause data loss", and advises converting only fields that have no data.

question: Cloud Kicks is implementing an approval process for opportunities that requires managers to approve all opportunities above $50,000 before they can be marked as Closed Won. Which two delivery methods can a manager utilize to respond to approval requests in the Salesforce mobile app? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Home Screen
optionC: Record Detail
explanation:
In the Salesforce mobile app, approval requests reach a manager as in-app (and push) notifications, and the manager can approve or reject from the record itself, where the Approval History related list carries the actions — Classic Approval Process Considerations for the Salesforce Mobile App notes that users "can see and take action from the Approval History related list". A caution on the option set: the same page also says "to respond to approval requests, go to the Approvals navigation item", so the navigation menu (option D) is a documented route too, and the two documented exclusions are Chatter ("you can't respond to approval requests from Chatter") and queues, which do not receive mobile notifications.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Home screen) — the mobile home page carries no approval controls.
Option D (Navigation menu) — the Approvals navigation item does list pending requests; this is a defensible answer the item does not credit.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.approvals_considerations_mobile_app.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: The dump keys in-app notifications and the record detail. Both are documented for the mobile app, but so is a third route the option set also offers: "To respond to approval requests, go to the Approvals navigation item" — the navigation menu (option D). Kept as keyed; treat this item as having three defensible options.

question: Sales reps at Universal Containers create multiple quotes per opportunity. What automation tool should an app builder recommend to delete rejected quotes?
optionA: Approval process
optionC: Workflow rule
explanation:
Flow is the declarative tool that can delete records: the Delete Records element lets a flow "identify Salesforce or Marketing Object records to delete by using the IDs stored in a record variable or record collection variable, or by specifying conditions." A record-triggered flow on Quote, firing when Status changes to Rejected, deletes the quote.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Approval process) — its automated actions are limited to task, email alert, field update and outbound message; it cannot delete.
Option B (Validation rule) — accepts or rejects a save; it never deletes anything.
Option C (Workflow rule) — offers field updates, email alerts, tasks and outbound messages; no delete action, and support for workflow rules ended on 31 December 2025.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_ref_elements_data_delete.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.automate_flow_build_get_started_record_triggered_flows.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The finance manager at Universal Containers wants to receive a new business notification email each time a new client is won. The sales manager wants to receive a task letting them know to onboard the new client unless it is a top-tier client. Which automation tool should an app builder use to best address all these requests?
optionA: Record-triggered flow
optionC: Apex
explanation:
A record-triggered flow on Opportunity handles both requests in one automation: when the stage becomes Closed Won, a Send Email (or email alert) action notifies the finance manager, and a Decision element checks the account tier before a Create Records element creates the onboarding task for the sales manager. The conditional branch is what a single flow does that simpler tools cannot.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Screen flow) — needs a user to click through screens; the requirement is automatic on save.
Option C (Apex) — code for something Flow Builder does declaratively.
Option D (Approval process) — routes a record for sign-off; there is no approval in the requirement.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.automate_flow_build_get_started_record_triggered_flows.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_ref_elements_actions_list.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An App Builder has been asked to integrate Salesforce with an external web service. The web service must be notified every time an Opportunity is Won. Which two can satisfy this requirement?
optionA: Use a workflow rule and an outbound message
optionB: Use a flow and an outbound message
optionC: Use a process and Apex Code
optionD: Use a process and an outbound message
explanation:
A workflow rule with an outbound message (option A) sends a SOAP notification to the web service when an opportunity is won, and a process that calls Apex (option C) can make any callout — those are the two the item credits. Read the option set with today's platform in mind, though: Send an Outbound Message from Your Record-Triggered Flow says "outbound messages are available as a core action in Flow Builder ... for record-triggered flows that run after the record is saved", so a flow with an outbound message (option B) also works now, and is the current recommendation since support for workflow rules and Process Builder ended on 31 December 2025.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (A flow and an outbound message) — correct on the current platform; the item predates the flow action, so the exam credits A and C.
Option D (A process and an outbound message) — Process Builder's action list has no outbound message action; outbound messages belonged to workflow rules and approval processes before they came to flows.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=release-notes.rn_automate_flow_builder_outbound_message.htm&language=en_US&release=234&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.process_action.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000389396&language=en_US&type=1

corrected.note: The exam key (workflow rule plus outbound message; process plus Apex) is kept, but the option set has aged: since the Winter '22 release "outbound messages are available as a core action in Flow Builder" for after-save record-triggered flows, so option B is also true today. Only option D is wrong — Process Builder has no outbound message action. Support for workflow rules and Process Builder ended on 31 December 2025.

question: Universal Containers has a customer base where many customers have the same or similar company names. Which functionality should be configured to improve an end user's search experience? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Update the account search layout's view filter settings.
optionB: Update the account search layouts search results columns displayed.
optionC: Update the account search filter fields.
optionD: Update the account search layouts accounts tab columns displayed.
explanation:
Two parts of the account search layout help users tell similar companies apart: the columns displayed on the search results page (option B) and the search filter fields (option C). Search Layout Guidelines lists both among what search layouts determine — "fields shown as columns on the search results page" and "fields users can filter to narrow what's shown on the search results page" — so adding fields such as billing city or account number lets users distinguish and filter the matches.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (The search layout's view filter settings) — not a search layout setting.
Option D (The accounts tab columns) — the Accounts tab list view is not the search results page.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.search_layout_guidelines.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers wants to track installation information on a custom object once a container has been purchased. Sales reps should have visibility of all the installations associated with their opportunities. What kind of relationship should this new object have to the Opportunity?
optionA: Lookup
optionC: Master-Detail
explanation:
A master-detail relationship to Opportunity gives the installations the visibility the requirement asks for. Custom Object Security explains how access to a detail record works: viewing one requires "Read permission and read access to the related master record", so a rep who can see the opportunity can see every installation under it, with no separate sharing to configure. Object Relationships Overview draws the contrast the other way: lookup relationships "don't support sharing or roll-up summary fields", so with a lookup the installations' visibility would be decided by the custom object's own org-wide default and sharing rules rather than by the opportunity.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Lookup) — links the records and gives a related list, but the installations' visibility would not follow the opportunity; a private org-wide default on the new object would hide them from the very reps the requirement names.
Option B (Hierarchical) — "a special lookup relationship available for only the user object."
Option D (Many to many) — needs a junction object between two masters; an installation belongs to one opportunity.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.overview_of_custom_object_relationships.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.dev_security.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: The dump keyed Lookup. The stated requirement is that reps who work an opportunity can see all of its installations, and Object Relationships Overview says lookup relationships "don't support sharing or roll-up summary fields" — record access on a lookup child is governed by that object's own org-wide default. A master-detail child is Controlled by Parent, so seeing the opportunity is seeing its installations. This is a judgment on which relationship best fits the stated visibility need; both relationships produce a related list.

question: The appraisal team at DreamHouse Realty wants to leverage Salesforce mobile app. What are three things an app builder should do to optimize mobile experience? Choose 3 answers.
optionA: Use Global Actions to make it easy to perform vital functionality on mobile.
optionB: Avoid using default field values so that the user is required to fill in all fields on the screen.
optionC: Minimize the amount of formula fields and lookup fields to reduce page load time.
optionD: Create individual customized layouts for different phone operating systems.
optionE: Put the most important fields in the compact layout so they are easy to find.
explanation:
Three mobile-first habits: use global actions so key tasks are one tap away anywhere in the app (option A) — global actions "can be added to almost any page that supports actions"; keep formula and lookup fields to a minimum so record pages load quickly on a phone (option C); and put the most important fields in the compact layout (option E), which is what "displays a record's key fields at a glance in the Salesforce mobile app." This is design guidance rather than a single documented rule; the references cover the two features named.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Avoid default values so users fill in every field) — the opposite of mobile-friendly; defaults reduce typing on a small screen.
Option D (Separate layouts per phone operating system) — the mobile app renders the same Lightning pages and layouts on iOS and Android; there is no per-OS layout.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.compact_layout_overview.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.actions_overview_global.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks (CK) captures all shipping information in a custom object called Shipments__c. CK's app builder is tasked with creating an approval process to ensure department members can approve all overnight shipments. Where should the app builder route the approval request?
optionA: Hierarchy field
optionC: Public group
explanation:
Route the step to a queue whose members are the department. Identify Assigned Approvers for an Approval Step offers "Automatically assign to a queue — available only for objects that support queues", and custom objects support queues; any queue member can then approve the overnight shipment. The other approver types on that page are the submitter's choice, a hierarchy field, and specific users or related users.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Hierarchy field) — routes to one user found in a field such as Manager, not to a whole department.
Option B (Role) — roles are not an approver type; the step cannot be assigned to a role.
Option C (Public group) — public groups are not an approver type either; groups are sharing constructs, and the approval step page does not list them.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.approvals_step_approver.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: The dump keyed a public group. Identify Assigned Approvers for an Approval Step lists the approver choices — the submitter, a hierarchy field, "automatically assign to a queue" ("available only for objects that support queues"), or specific users and related users — and public groups are not among them. A custom object such as Shipments__c supports queues, so a queue of the department members is the documented way to let any of them approve.

question: Universal Containers has a Lightning record page that supports both the mobile app and desktop. An app builder has downloaded a custom Lightning component from AppExchange, but users are unable to view the component on mobile devices. What can be the issue?
optionA: The record page needs to be activated.
optionB: The component has been developed for Desktop Pages.
optionC: The component needs to be activated.
optionD: The record page template is unable to support mobile devices.
explanation:
The component was built for desktop only. Custom Lightning components declare which form factors they support — Visibility Rules on Lightning Pages notes that "custom Lightning components can also be set to support different form factors" — and a component whose bundle targets only the desktop (Large) form factor is dropped from the page on a phone even though the page itself supports both.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (The record page needs to be activated) — an inactive page would be missing on desktop too, and the stem says desktop users see it.
Option C (The component needs to be activated) — components are not activated; pages are.
Option D (The page template can't support mobile) — the stem says the page supports both the mobile app and desktop.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.lightning_page_components_visibility.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: UVC's CFO has asked that all deals with more than a 40% discount get automatically sent to the VP of Finance. He will review these deals without the sales rep needing to take action. Which two ways can this be accomplished without building code? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Launch a new approval process that has automatic submission enabled as an initial submission action
optionB: Create a new process with a submit for approval action to automatically submit deals for approval
optionC: Create a new approval process that has automatic submission enabled in the entry criteria
optionD: Launch a flow that uses the submit for approval action to submit deals for approval
explanation:
Automatic submission comes from an automation that calls the Submit for Approval action when the discount exceeds 40%: a process built in Process Builder with a Submit for Approval action (option B) or a record-triggered flow using the Submit for Approval core action (option D). Provided Flow Core Actions lists "Submit for Approval Action" among the Salesforce-provided actions, and Add Actions to Your Process lists it for processes. Note that support for Process Builder ended on 31 December 2025, so the flow is the current build.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (An approval process with automatic submission as an initial submission action) — initial submission actions run after a record is submitted; no action submits the record itself.
Option C (An approval process with automatic submission in the entry criteria) — entry criteria decide whether a submitted record enters the process; they do not submit it.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_ref_elements_actions_list.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.process_action.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: The dump keyed two options describing an "automatic submission" setting on the approval process, which does not exist — a classic approval process has no setting that submits records on its own. What submits a record without the rep acting is the Submit for Approval action, available in Process Builder and as a provided flow core action.

question: Service Agents are required to confirm a user's identity before providing support information over the phone. Which feature can an app builder use to help agents meet this requirement?
optionA: Guided Action Flows on the record page
optionB: Add Path to the top of the Case layout
optionC: Include Surveys as a Case related list
explanation:
The Actions & Recommendations component (guided action flows) puts an identity-verification screen flow on the case page as a step agents follow: "Give your users a to-do list in the Actions & Recommendations component. Show a variety of steps, including screen flows ... quick actions, and recommendations." A screen flow can ask the caller's security questions and record the result before the agent continues.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Path on the case layout) — shows stage guidance text; it cannot run a verification dialogue.
Option C (Surveys as a related list) — surveys collect feedback after the fact; they are not an agent-side verification step.
Option D (Case validation rules) — validate field values on save; they cannot guide a live verification.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.lightning_page_components.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_actions.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which three Salesforce functionalities are ignored when processing field updates in workflow rules and approval processes? Choose 3 answers.
optionA: Multiple currencies
optionC: Validation Rules
explanation:
Field updates run as the system, so two safeguards that apply to users do not apply to them. Considerations for Field Update Actions: "Field updates function independently of field-level security. Therefore, a workflow rule can update fields even though they're hidden on the user's page layout" (option B), and "updates to records based on workflow rules and also on process-scheduled actions don't trigger validation rules" (option C). The third credited item, decimal places and character limits (option E), is the exam's answer; it is not stated on the current page, so treat it as the item's claim rather than a documented fact.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Multiple currencies) — currency is respected: "if your organization uses multiple currencies, currency fields are updated using the record's currency."
Option D (Record type picklist value assignments) — not on the current page either; of the two undocumented candidates the exam credits E.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.workflow_field_update_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Two of the three keyed items are on Considerations for Field Update Actions today — "field updates function independently of field-level security" and "updates to records based on workflow rules ... don't trigger validation rules." The third, decimal places and character limits, is not stated on any current Salesforce page, and neither is the record-type alternative (option D); the item rests on documentation that has since been rewritten. Kept as keyed.

question: Ursa Major Solar wants to provide sales console users with an incredible experience, with the most-used components easily accessible at all times. What solution can enable reps to see and access these components from anywhere within the app without leaving the pages where the team is working?
optionA: Favorites
optionC: Global actions
explanation:
The utility bar keeps the most-used components available from every page in the app: it "gives your users quick access to common productivity tools, like Notes and Recent Items. It appears as a fixed footer that users can access to open utilities in docked panels", and it is configured per Lightning app, including console apps.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Favorites) — bookmarks to records, lists and pages; navigating to one leaves the current page.
Option B (Home page) — one page among many; reps would have to go there.
Option C (Global actions) — create or log records from the action menu; they are not a place to dock reusable components.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.apps_lightning_utilities.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The marketing team at UVC has a list of 400 leads it wants to upload to Salesforce. The team needs to avoid creating duplicate records. Which two actions should be taken to meet this requirement? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Utilize a Lead Matching Rule and corresponding Duplicate Rule to block newly created duplicate leads.
optionB: Upload the lead list using the import wizard and select a Matching type to prevent duplicate lead creation.
optionC: Use Data Loader's update function to import lead and match to existing records based on e-mail address.
optionD: Enable Duplicate Matching in the Data Management section in Setup and activate the Lead-to-Lead scenario.
explanation:
Two independent guards: a lead matching rule with a duplicate rule whose action is Block stops duplicate leads at creation, including leads created by an import (option A), and the Data Import Wizard's own matching type prevents them at load time (option B) — What Is Imported for Leads?: "Leads can be matched according to the following types: Salesforce ID, name, email, or external ID. Choosing a matching type sets the criteria for avoiding duplicate leads", so a lead in the file that matches an existing one is updated rather than created.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option C (Data Loader's update function matched on email) — Data Loader's update needs the Salesforce record ID, not an email address, and an update would skip genuinely new leads instead of inserting them; the tool for 400 records is the import wizard anyway.
Option D (Enable Duplicate Matching in Data Management and activate a Lead-to-Lead scenario) — not how duplicate management is configured; the features are matching rules and duplicate rules under Duplicate Management in Setup.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.duplicate_rules_create.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.for_leads.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers wants to streamline its data capture process by linking fields together. They wish to do this so that the available values on dependent fields are driven by the value selected on controlling fields. Which considerations support the stated requirements? Choose 3 answers.
optionA: The import wizard only allows values to be imported into a dependent picklist if they match the appropriate controlling field.
optionB: Custom picklist fields can be either controlling or dependent fields.
optionC: Multi-select picklists can be dependent picklists but not controlling fields.
optionD: Standard and custom picklist fields can be dependent fields.
optionE: Checkbox fields can be controlling fields but not dependent fields
explanation:
Three of these statements are on Dependent Picklist Considerations word for word: "Custom picklist fields can be either controlling or dependent fields" (option B), "Multi-select picklists can be dependent picklists but not controlling fields" (option C), and "Checkbox fields can be controlling fields but not dependent fields" (option E).
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (The import wizard only allows dependent values that match the controlling field) — the same page says "The Data Import Wizard doesn't consider field dependencies. You can import any value into a dependent picklist regardless of the value imported for a controlling field."
Option D (Standard and custom picklists can be dependent) — "Standard picklist fields can be controlling fields but not dependent fields."
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_dependent_field_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: The dump keyed the import-wizard statement as true. Dependent Picklist Considerations says the opposite: "The Data Import Wizard doesn't consider field dependencies. You can import any value into a dependent picklist regardless of the value imported for a controlling field." The three documented truths are that custom picklists can be either role, multi-select picklists can be dependent but not controlling, and checkboxes can be controlling but not dependent.

question: An app builder wants to create a formula field on an Account to include data from related Contacts but is unable to find the relationship in the formula editor. What is a limitation of formulas that could be causing the issue?
optionA: Unable to reference the child records.
optionB: A master-detail relationship should be created.
optionC: Formula field limit reached on the Account object.
optionD: More than 5,000 characters in the formula.
explanation:
Formulas cannot reference child records. What Is a Cross-Object Formula? defines the direction: a cross-object formula "can reference merge fields from a master ('parent') object if an object is on the detail side of a master-detail relationship" and "also works with lookup relationships" — from the child up to the parent, "up to 10 relationships away." Contacts are children of Account, so the formula editor on Account offers no path to them; a roll-up summary or a report is the tool for summarising children.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (A master-detail relationship should be created) — the relationship type does not change the direction formulas can span; even master-detail children are unreachable from a parent formula.
Option C (Formula field limit reached) — a limit would stop the field being saved, not hide a relationship in the editor.
Option D (More than 5,000 characters) — a size limit on the formula text, unrelated to which relationships appear.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.customize_cross_object.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_creating_cross_object_notes.htm&language=en_US&type=5
