question: The developer at Universal Containers wants to test code in a sandbox environment. In order to ensure the code works properly, the sandbox needs to have at least half a gigabyte of data. The sandbox will need to be refreshed after each three-day sprint. What type of sandbox should the app builder provision to the developer?
optionA: Developer
optionC: Developer Pro
explanation:
A Developer Pro sandbox meets both constraints: a 1-day refresh interval, so it can be refreshed after every three-day sprint, and 1 GB of data storage, enough for the half gigabyte of test data the developer loads. Sandbox Licenses and Storage Limits by Type gives those figures.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Developer) — refreshes daily but holds only 200 MB, short of the half gigabyte.
Option B (Full Copy) — 29-day refresh interval.
Option D (Partial Copy) — 5-day refresh interval, so it cannot follow a three-day sprint cadence, and it needs a template rather than developer-loaded data.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.data_sandbox_environments.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: The dump keyed Partial Copy. Sandbox Licenses and Storage Limits by Type gives Partial Copy a 5-day refresh interval, so it cannot be refreshed after every three-day sprint. Developer Pro refreshes daily and holds 1 GB of data, which covers the half gigabyte the developer needs.

question: A sales manager has noticed that reps continue to input contacts directly in their phone instead of adding them to Salesforce. What should an app builder recommend to ensure the data makes it into Salesforce?
optionA: Enable in-app notifications every time a contact is created.
optionB: Allow Salesforce to import Contacts from mobile device Contact lists.
optionC: Enable offline create, edit, and delete in Salesforce for Android and iOS.
optionD: Allow users to relate a contact to multiple accounts.
explanation:
Enabling offline create, edit and delete lets reps add contacts in the Salesforce mobile app even without a connection, which removes the reason they fall back to the phone's own contact list. Enable Offline Access and Offline Edit: "to allow updating records while offline, select Enable offline create, edit, and delete in Salesforce for Android and iOS", and the changes sync when connectivity returns.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (In-app notifications when a contact is created) — notifies after the fact; it does not make entry easier.
Option B (Import contacts from the device's contact list) — the Salesforce mobile app has no such import; it is not a documented feature.
Option D (Relate a contact to multiple accounts) — a data-model feature (Contacts to Multiple Accounts) unrelated to where reps enter contacts.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.salesforce_app_enable_offline_access.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: DreamHouse Realty (DR) has many properties for sale and wants to identify the highest value of all Offer__c records on each Property__c record. What solution should the app builder use to meet DreamHouse Realty's needs?
optionA: Master-Detail Child Object
optionC: Multi-select Picklist
explanation:
Make Offer__c a master-detail child of Property__c and add a MAX roll-up summary field. Roll-Up Summary Field: "you can calculate the sum, minimum value, or maximum value of a field in the detail records", with "number, currency, percent, date, and date/time fields ... available when you select MIN or MAX", and "the detail record must be related to the master through a master-detail relationship."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Text Area Long) — a free-text field cannot compute anything.
Option C (Multi-select picklist) — a fixed value list, not a calculation.
Option D (Lookup object) — lookups "don't support ... roll-up summary fields", so the maximum could not be calculated declaratively.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_roll_up_summary_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A customer service representative at a call center wants to be able to collect information from customers using a series of question prompts. What should an app builder use to accomplish this?
optionA: Approval Process
optionC: Validation Rule
explanation:
A screen flow presents a series of screens with question prompts and stores the answers, which is exactly a guided call script for a representative; it can be launched from a quick action on the case or contact record ("users can run a screen flow with the click of a button on a Lightning record page").
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Approval process) — routes a record for sign-off; it asks nothing of a caller.
Option C (Validation rule) — checks values at save; it has no screens.
Option D (Path) — shows stage guidance text; it cannot prompt and capture answers.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_actions.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_ref_elements_actions_list.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers uses a custom picklist called Account_Region__c on the Account object. The vice president of sales has asked that the value of this field is visible on Opportunities. How should an app builder create this solution?
optionA: Lookup field
optionC: Field history tracking
explanation:
A cross-object formula field on Opportunity displays the Account's picklist: TEXT(Account.Account_Region__c). What Is a Cross-Object Formula? — "a cross-object formula can reference merge fields from a master ('parent') object" and "also works with lookup relationships", which Opportunity to Account is.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Lookup field) — Opportunity already looks up to Account; a lookup shows a record link, not a field value from it.
Option B (Field-level security) — controls who can see a field; it cannot make an Account field appear on Opportunity.
Option C (Field history tracking) — records changes to a field over time; it does not display a parent value.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.customize_cross_object.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers wants to ensure that they are accepting clean data from their users and verify that important fields are entered. What should an app builder recommend to meet this requirement?
optionA: Update the important fields to be required on the page layout
optionB: Make a formula field to check the format of the important fields
optionC: Create a workflow rule to check the fields are formatted correctly
optionD: Configure a validation rule to require a field for a specific record type.
explanation:
A validation rule that requires the field for a specific record type both verifies that important fields are entered and lets the requirement differ by record type — a formula such as AND($RecordType.DeveloperName = "Enterprise", ISBLANK(Important_Field__c)) blocks the save with a clear message. Validation rules are the one tool that can enforce data quality conditionally on every entry path, including the API and imports.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Required on the page layout) — enforced only through that layout's UI, not through the API or Data Loader, and it cannot vary by record type without a second layout.
Option B (A formula field to check the format) — a formula displays a result; it cannot stop a save.
Option C (A workflow rule to check formatting) — workflow rules act after a valid save; they cannot reject data.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_validation_rules_tips.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_validation_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Properly installing managed packages helps prevent conflicts with customizations made by customers and partners. What functionality should be used to set up packages?
optionA: Description
optionC: Help setting
explanation:
A namespace is what keeps a managed package's components from colliding with the subscriber's own: it is a globally unique one-to-15-character prefix that "distinguishes your package and its contents from packages of other developers", and every object, field and class in the package carries it (for example pkg__Invoice__c), so a customer's Invoice__c and the package's cannot clash.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Description) — documentation text; it prevents nothing.
Option B (Allow sharing) — not a packaging setting.
Option C (Help setting) — points users to help content; unrelated to naming conflicts.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pkg1-dev/guide/register-namespace-prefix.html
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.distribution_installing_packages.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An app builder wants to limit the number of fields users are required to fill out when creating a new Opportunity. Once they fill out the required fields and save, the full record page with additional fields relevant to the Opportunity type becomes available. How could this be accomplished?
optionA: Make the Opportunity type a required field on the initial Opportunity page layout and use automation to fill in the type field to a record type.
optionB: Use different page layouts for Opportunity types based on the user profile.
optionC: Once the required fields are populated, use a sharing rule to share the new fields with the user.
optionD: Hide additional sections on the page layout and show the users how to manually expand them when they want to fill in the fields in the hidden sections.
explanation:
Record types with their own page layouts are the declarative way to show a short form first and a fuller one later: make Opportunity Type required on the initial layout, and let automation set the record type from the chosen type so the record then opens on the layout that carries the type-specific fields. Page layouts are assigned by record type and profile, which is why the record type has to change for the layout to change.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Layouts by user profile) — a profile does not change after the record is saved, so the same user would keep seeing the same short layout.
Option C (A sharing rule to share the new fields) — sharing rules grant record access; they cannot reveal fields.
Option D (Hidden sections users expand manually) — sections cannot be hidden on a page layout, and manual expansion is not the automatic behaviour asked for.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.users_profiles_record_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Accounts at Universal Containers are currently readable by all users but editable only by their owners. Management wants to designate some Accounts as VIP Accounts. Only Account owners should have read access to these VIP accounts. Which two actions should an app builder take to meet the requirements? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Implement a sharing rule.
optionC: Set up an Account Team.
explanation:
Two changes: set the Account org-wide default to Private so only owners see their accounts (option D), then add an owner-based sharing rule that shares the non-VIP accounts with everyone (option A). Org-wide defaults set the baseline; sharing rules can only open access, never restrict it — so the current Public Read Only default cannot be narrowed for the VIP accounts alone, and the whole object has to go Private with a rule opening the rest back up.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (A permission set) — object permissions such as View All would widen access, and no permission set can hide specific records.
Option C (An Account Team) — teams add access for named users on individual accounts; they cannot take read access away from the users who currently have it.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_sharing_owd_about.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_sharing_rules_owner.htm&type=5&language=en_US

question: Universal Containers created a 'New Task' custom action on the Opportunity object. The action was added to all page layouts in the Mobile & Lightning Actions section. Which Lightning component should the app builder add to the layout to display the action?
optionA: Related record
optionC: Highlights panel
explanation:
The Activities component is where a task-creating quick action surfaces. Actions in Lightning Experience is explicit: "The Activity tab contains Create a Record quick actions that point to the Event and Task objects. It also contains Log A Call and Send Email actions", and of the highlights panel it says "although they're quick actions, New Event and New Task don't show up here." The page-layout action list feeds both places, but each action is routed by its target object, and a custom New Task action targets Task.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Related Record) — shows a related record's details and offers that object's update action; it does not display the page layout's action list.
Option B (Related Lists) — carry the related object's own buttons, not page-level actions.
Option C (Highlights Panel) — shows the page-level action menu, from which the documentation excludes task and event actions.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.actions_in_lex.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.lightning_page_components.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: The dump keyed the Highlights Panel. Actions in Lightning Experience routes task-creating actions elsewhere: 'The Activity tab contains Create a Record quick actions that point to the Event and Task objects', and 'although they're quick actions, New Event and New Task don't show up' in the highlights panel's page-level action menu. A custom New Task action is a Create a Record action targeting Task, so the Activities component is where it appears.

question: Universal Containers is piloting new features in an existing sandbox and wants to prevent outbound email sends during testing. What should the app builder do to meet the requirement?
optionA: Email deliverability set to system email only.
optionC: Email relay to the configured host enabled.
optionD: Email deliverability set to no access.
explanation:
Set the sandbox's email deliverability access level to No access. Email Deliverability: "No access — allows only password reset emails. Prevents all other outbound email to and from users", which is what a pilot that must not email anyone needs. New and refreshed sandboxes default to System email only.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (System email only) — still "allows only automatically generated emails, such as new user and password reset emails"; it blocks user-sent mail but not all outbound email.
Option B (SMTP authentication) — a relay-security setting; it does not stop email.
Option C (Email relay enabled) — routes outbound mail through a host; the opposite of preventing it.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.data_sandbox_email_deliverability.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers would like to automatically assign a specific permission set to new users. How can this requirement be met? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Create an approval process on the User object to assign a permission set
optionB: Create a flow on the user object to assign a permission set.
optionC: Create a Lightning process on the User object to launch a flow.
optionD: Create a workflow rule on the User object to assign a permission set.
explanation:
A permission set is assigned by creating a PermissionSetAssignment record, which a flow can do with a Create Records element. Two declarative routes therefore work: a record-triggered flow on the User object that creates the assignment when a user is created (option B), or a process on the User object that launches that flow (option C) — "launch a flow" is one of the process actions. Support for Process Builder ended on 31 December 2025, so the flow alone is the current build.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (An approval process on User) — approvals route records for sign-off; their actions cannot create an assignment record.
Option D (A workflow rule on User) — workflow actions are field update, email alert, task and outbound message; none creates a record.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.automate_flow_build_get_started_record_triggered_flows.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.process_action.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers conducts evaluations of its sales reps using a custom object consisting of numerical scores and executive comments. The company wants to ensure that only the sales rep and their managers and executives can view the rep's evaluation record, but the reps should not be able to view the executive comment field on their review. How can these requirements be met?
optionA: Use a private sharing model granting record access using hierarchy; manage field access with record types and field-level security
optionB: Use a private sharing model granting record access using custom setting; manage field access with page layouts and field level security
optionC: Use a private sharing model granting record access using hierarchy; manage field access with field-level security
optionD: Use a private sharing model granting record access using custom setting; manage field access with record types and page layouts
explanation:
A private sharing model on the evaluation object, with Grant Access Using Hierarchies on, lets the rep (as owner) and the managers and executives above them in the role hierarchy see the record; field-level security then hides the executive comment field from the rep's profile while leaving it visible to management. Two layers, two tools: sharing for the record, field permissions for the field.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Hierarchy plus record types and field-level security) — record types control picklist values and layouts, not who can see a field; only the field-level security part does any work.
Option B (Custom setting plus page layouts and field-level security) — custom settings are configuration data, not a sharing mechanism, and page layouts do not secure fields.
Option D (Custom setting plus record types and page layouts) — none of the three grants record access or hides a field.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_sharing_owd_about.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.security_controlling_access_using_hierarchies.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.users_profiles_field_perms.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: What are two capabilities of Schema Builder? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Editing custom settings
optionC: Showing selected objects on a page
optionD: Viewing page layouts in a new window
explanation:
Schema Builder shows exactly the objects you select on its canvas (option C) — "select the checkbox for the object ... to display it on the canvas", and its View menu filters between all, selected, standard, custom and system objects. The exam also credits editing custom settings (option A): custom settings are list or hierarchy objects that Schema Builder can display and whose fields can be added there, though the current documentation describes the tool in terms of custom objects, fields and relationships and does not name custom settings explicitly.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Creating a new record type) — record types are created in Object Manager; Schema Builder has no record-type element.
Option D (Viewing page layouts in a new window) — Schema Builder does not show page layouts at all, which is why a field added there "isn't automatically added to the object's page layout."
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.schema_builder_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.schema_builder.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Showing selected objects on the canvas is documented; editing custom settings is the exam's answer for the second capability but is not stated on the current Schema Builder pages, which describe custom objects, fields and relationships. The other two options are clearly outside Schema Builder (record types, page layouts), so the keyed pair is the only defensible one. Kept as keyed.

question: Universal Containers has a new custom object for Invoices that includes an Invoice Number field, Before the Invoice object can be used, invoices will be migrated from an external system maintaining their current Invoice Number. After the migration, salesforce will be the system of record and each new Invoice created in Salesforce must have a unique Invoice Number. How should the app builder configure the Invoice Number field?
optionA: Create a Text field for the original Invoice Number and an Auto Number field for the Salesforce Invoice Number.
optionB: Create a Text field and mark it as a unique external ID field.
optionC: Create a Text field, then change it to Auto Number after the migration.
optionD: Create an Auto Number field and migrate the Invoices.
explanation:
A Text field marked Unique and External ID serves both phases. Custom Field Attributes: an external ID "contains record identifiers from a system outside of Salesforce", is available on text, number, email and auto-number fields, and "you can use this field to prevent duplicates by also marking the field as Unique" — so the migrated invoice numbers load unchanged and every later invoice must carry a unique value.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Text for the original plus Auto Number for the Salesforce number) — two numbers per invoice, when the requirement is one Invoice Number that stays the same after migration.
Option C (Text, then change to Auto Number after migration) — an auto-number field generates new values in its display format; converting after the fact would not keep the migrated numbers as the unique key, and the uniqueness requirement is met by the Unique attribute, not by a type change.
Option D (Auto Number and migrate) — an auto-number field assigns its own values, so the external system's invoice numbers could not be preserved.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.custom_field_attributes.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.notes_on_changing_custom_field_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Managers at Universal Containers want a quick way to create additional accounts to form a hierarchy from a parent account record. They want to auto-populate five fields based on the parent to make it easier for users to create the child accounts quickly. What should an app builder create to meet this requirement?
optionA: Custom Global Quick Action
optionC: Custom action on Account
explanation:
A custom object-specific Create a Record action on Account, with predefined field values, creates the child account from the parent record with five fields already filled in. Object-Specific Actions: an action created on the Account object creates records "in the context of a particular object", and Set Predefined Field Values for Quick Action Fields is where the five defaults are configured.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Custom global quick action) — "global create actions enable users to create object records, but the new record has no direct relationship with other records", so the parent link and its values would be lost.
Option B (Custom global quick action layout) — the layout of a global action has the same limitation.
Option D (Custom link on Account) — opens a URL; it cannot prepopulate a new record's fields the way an action's predefined values do.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.actions_overview_object_specific.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.predefined_field_values.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers requires different fields to be filled out at each stage of the Opportunity sales process. What configuration steps can an app builder use to meet this requirement?
optionA: Set page layout required fields based on the current stage.
optionB: Create a Process Builder to prompt the User for field information.
optionC: Define record types and page layouts for each stage.
optionD: Add the Path component to the Lightning record page.
explanation:
Path, added to the Lightning record page, is the configuration that surfaces different key fields at each stage of the sales process — up to five per stage, with guidance text. Read the requirement carefully, though: Path guides rather than enforces. Considerations and Guidelines for Creating Paths says "you can't use the page layout to require different fields in different steps. However, you can set up validation rules based on a path step", so making the fields mandatory per stage takes a validation rule alongside the Path.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Page layout required fields based on the current stage) — a page layout has one set of required fields regardless of stage; the documentation says this cannot be done.
Option B (A Process Builder to prompt the user) — processes run after save and have no user interface to prompt with.
Option C (Record types and page layouts per stage) — record types are chosen at creation, not switched as a deal advances; using them per stage is not a supported pattern.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.path_overview.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.path_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers wants to understand return on investment for the latest advertising buy. They currently use a private security model for all objects. What should an app builder recommend?
optionA: Utilize Account Hierarchies and Roll-Up Summary fields
optionC: Change to a public security model
optionD: Configure Campaign Hierarchies and Campaign statistics
explanation:
Campaign hierarchies with campaign statistics are built for exactly this: "metrics from child campaigns roll up to the parent, so you can access data for individual campaigns or in aggregate." The private sharing model is not an obstacle either — "a parent campaign's statistics include aggregate values based on all its child campaigns, regardless of the current user's sharing settings."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Account hierarchies and roll-up summary fields) — accounts group customers, not marketing spend; the advertising buy is a campaign.
Option B (Opportunity pipeline report) — shows open deals, not the return on a specific campaign.
Option C (Change to a public security model) — unnecessary, since campaign statistics aggregate regardless of sharing, and it would loosen security for no reason.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.campaigns_hierarchy.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Ursa Major Solar (UMS) is planning to hire some new employees. UMS wants to allow a job candidate (Job_Candidate__c) to apply for multiple open positions (Open_Position__c) and then be able to view the applications (Application__c) on the job candidate record. UMS also wants to view all the applications for a specific open position. What should an app builder recommend to meet these requirements? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Create a master-detail relationship on Open_Position__c to Application__c.
optionB: Create a master-detail relationship field on Job_Candidate__c to Application__c.
optionC: Create a master-detail relationship field on Application__c to Job_Candidate__c.
optionD: Create a master-detail relationship field on Application__c to Open_Position__c.
explanation:
Application__c is the junction object, so it carries a master-detail relationship to each master: one to Job_Candidate__c (option C) and one to Open_Position__c (option D). That is the documented many-to-many pattern — "you use a junction object to connect the two objects you want to relate to each other" — and it gives both masters a related list of applications, which is exactly the two views UMS asked for.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Master-detail on Open_Position__c to Application__c) — the relationship field lives on the detail (junction) side; a master cannot hold the master-detail field.
Option B (Master-detail on Job_Candidate__c to Application__c) — same mistake in the other direction.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.overview_of_custom_object_relationships.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.relationships_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers uses Contracts for agreements with customers. A sales manager is required to provide approval for contracts and director approval for any contract over $10,000. Which two options should an app builder use to ensure all contracts route for the correct approval and also prevent the sales rep from making changes to the record while it is being approved? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Create an approval process on the Contract object with criteria set on a second approval step set as 'Amount__c > 10,000' and set the approver as director.
optionB: Create an approval process on the Contract object and set the field for 'Next Automated Approver Determined By' as Manager'.
optionC: Create a validation rule on the Contract object that prevents updates to the contract record while it is being reviewed.
optionD: Create an approval process on the Contract object with one step for each sales manager that sets the approver as the director.
explanation:
Two settings inside the approval process do everything the requirement asks. Setting Next Automated Approver Determined By to the Manager field lets the first step "route approval requests to the submitting user's manager" (option B), and a second step with criteria of Amount__c > 10,000 and the director as approver adds the extra sign-off only for large contracts (option A). The edit restriction needs nothing extra: "when a record is submitted for approval, it's locked to prevent users from editing it during the classic approval process."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option C (A validation rule to prevent updates during review) — redundant; submitted records are locked by the approval process itself, and who may edit a locked record is a record-editability setting of the process.
Option D (One step per sales manager assigned to the director) — one step per manager does not scale and never routes to the manager at all; the Manager hierarchy field does that in one step.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.approvals_create_automatedfield.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.approvals_create_recordeditability.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.approvals_step_approver.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: The dump keyed a validation rule to stop edits during approval. That is unnecessary: "when a record is submitted for approval, it's locked to prevent users from editing it during the classic approval process." The two configuration choices that route the request correctly are a second step with entry criteria of Amount__c > 10,000 assigned to the director, and Next Automated Approver Determined By set to the Manager field so the first step goes to the submitter's manager.

question: A user is unable to use inline editing on a list view. A quick check verifies the user should be able to perform inline editing as they have been assigned the appropriate permissions. Which two conditions should the app builder review? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: If the list view restricts sharing for the user
optionB: If the list view selected is the recently viewed list view
optionC: If the list view contains a chart created by the user
optionD: If the list view contains more than one record type
explanation:
Two list-view conditions block inline editing. Considerations for Inline Editing in a List View: "by default, list views and multiline views that contain more than one record type aren't inline editable" (option D), and the predefined Recently Viewed list is editable only when it "is predefined to contain only one record type", so on an object with several record types the Recently Viewed list cannot be edited inline (option B). A filter on a single record type restores editing.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (The list view restricts sharing for the user) — list views do not change sharing; a record the user cannot edit shows a lock icon, but the stem says the user has the right permissions.
Option C (The list view contains a chart) — charts display beside the list and have no effect on editing.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.basics_customviews_lv_lex_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: After Universal Containers converts qualified leads, sales reps need to be able to report on converted leads. How should an app builder support this requirement?
optionA: Enable preserve lead status in the lead conversion settings
optionB: Assign the representative view and edit converted leads permission
optionC: Ensure the representative has read access to the original lead records
optionD: Create a custom report type with converted leads as the primary object
explanation:
The View and Edit Converted Leads permission is what sales reps need. Converted leads already appear in standard lead reports — "standard Lead Reports in Salesforce display both active and converted Leads by default", and a Converted equals True filter isolates them — but a rep cannot open a converted lead from the report without the permission: "to view the converted Lead record directly, the admin must assign the View and Edit Converted Leads permission to the user."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Enable Preserve Lead Status) — a lead-conversion setting that keeps the lead's status on conversion; it has no bearing on reporting or access.
Option C (Read access to the original lead records) — reps already have object access to leads; converted records are hidden by the conversion, not by sharing, and only the permission reveals them.
Option D (A custom report type with converted leads as the primary object) — converted leads are not a separate object, and standard lead reports already include them.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000004948&language=en_US&type=1

corrected.note: The dump keyed a custom report type "with converted leads as the primary object" — there is no such object, and none is needed: Converted Leads Displayed in Leads Report says "standard Lead Reports in Salesforce display both active and converted Leads by default." What a rep lacks is the ability to open the converted lead records the report lists: "to view the converted Lead record directly, the admin must assign the View and Edit Converted Leads permission to the user." That permission is the only option that changes what reps can do.

question: Universal Containers uses a private sharing model for opportunities. This model CANNOT be changed due to a regional structure. A new sales operations team has been created. This team needs to perform analysis on Opportunity data, and all should have read and write access to all Opportunities. What are two recommended solutions for the app builder to give the users appropriate access? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Create a criteria-based sharing rule to all opportunities with the sales operations public group.
optionB: Add a manual share for all opportunities with each user on the sales operations team.
optionC: Add a permission set with "View All" and "Modify All" opportunity permissions enabled.
optionD: Create a criteria-based sharing rule to share all opportunities with the sales operations private group
explanation:
Two mechanisms give a team read and write access to every opportunity without changing the private default: a criteria-based sharing rule that shares all opportunities with the sales operations public group (option A), or a permission set with the "View All" and "Modify All" object permissions for Opportunity (option C). The View All and Modify All permissions bypass sharing settings for an object, which is exactly what an analysis team needs.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Manual shares on every opportunity) — one-off, record by record, and lost when ownership changes; unworkable for "all opportunities".
Option D (Share with a private group) — sharing rules share with public groups, roles and territories; there is no private group type.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.security_sharing_rules_criteria.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.users_profiles_view_all_mod_all.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.perm_sets_overview.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers' app builder has been tasked with replacing workflow rules and Apex triggers with Process Builders where possible. What are two important considerations an app builder should know before the project is started? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Avoid generating infinite loops.
optionB: Apex has a different SOQL query limit than Flow.
optionC: Create a process for each workflow rule.
explanation:
Two considerations from Salesforce's own Process Builder guidance: avoid creating an infinite loop — "avoid creating an infinite loop when allowing your process to reevaluate records", the example being a process whose Chatter post re-fires on every reevaluation — (option A), and consolidate: "have only one record-change process per object", which combines the actions of several workflow rules into one process with explicit ordering (option D). Note that support for Process Builder ended on 31 December 2025; a project starting today would migrate to Flow Builder instead.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Apex has a different SOQL query limit than Flow) — both run inside the same transaction governor limits; the SOQL limit is per transaction, not per tool.
Option C (Create a process for each workflow rule) — the opposite of the documented best practice of one record-change process per object.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.process_advanced_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.process_considerations_design_bestpractices.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000389396&language=en_US&type=1

question: What option is available to an App Builder when defining an object-specific Create Record custom action? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: Pre-Defining field values on the target object.
optionB: Redirecting the end user to the detail page of the target object
optionC: Specifying the fields and layout of the action.
optionD: Allowing the end user to choose the record type
explanation:
When defining an object-specific Create a Record action an app builder can set predefined field values on the target object (option A) and choose the fields and layout of the action (option C). Set Predefined Field Values for Quick Action Fields covers the first; the action layout editor, and for page-based quick actions the Lightning App Builder where "you configure the fields, sections, visibility rules, and layout", covers the second.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Redirect the user to the new record's detail page) — a create action shows a success message and keeps the user on the current page; the redirect behaviour is not a configurable option.
Option D (Let the user choose the record type) — a create action is bound to one record type when it is defined; the user does not pick it at run time.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.actions_overview_object_specific.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.predefined_field_values.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An app builder at Ursa Major Solar has been working on a new custom app in a sandbox that has been upgraded to the next major Salesforce version, and their production instance is still on the current Salesforce version. The development is complete and they are ready to deploy a change set. What should the app builder consider when planning the deployment?
optionA: It will fail if there is a feature only available in the next version.
optionB: The change set components will be upgraded to the next version in production.
optionC: The change set will be automatically deployed when production is upgraded.
optionD: The deployment is not possible due to different versions.
explanation:
The deployment can fail if the change set uses anything that exists only in the newer release. A preview sandbox is upgraded about six weeks ahead of production — Salesforce Sandbox Preview Instructions describes the preview window in which sandboxes are on the new release while "production and non-preview instances are upgraded to the new release around 6 weeks after" — so a component built on a new-release feature, field or API version has no counterpart in production and the deployment fails, the same way Change Sets Best Practices says a deployment fails when a component "refers to another component missing from the target org." Components that use only current-release functionality deploy normally. The documentation states the preview timing rather than the change-set rule itself, so the references are orienting.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Components are upgraded to the next version in production) — production stays on its release until Salesforce upgrades it; a change set cannot advance it.
Option C (The change set deploys automatically when production is upgraded) — change sets never deploy on their own.
Option D (Deployment is not possible because of different versions) — deployment from a preview sandbox works for components that do not depend on new-release features.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000391927&language=en_US&type=1
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.changesets_best_practices.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which two solutions prevent a formula field from being referenced by a Roll-Up Summary Field? Choose 2 answers.
optionA: A cross-object workflow updating a field referenced by the formula field
optionB: A cross-object field reference in the formula field
optionC: The CASE () function in the formula field
optionD: The NOW () function in the formula field
explanation:
Roll-Up Summary Field names both exclusions: "automatically derived fields, such as current date or current user, aren't allowed in a roll-up summary field. Forbidden fields include formula fields containing functions that derive values on the fly, such as DATEVALUE, NOW, and TODAY. Formula fields that include related object merge fields are also not allowed in roll-up summary fields." So a cross-object reference (option B) and NOW() (option D) each disqualify the formula.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (A cross-object workflow updating a field the formula references) — what updates a source field has no bearing on whether the formula itself can be rolled up.
Option C (CASE() in the formula) — CASE evaluates stored values; it is not a function that derives a value on the fly, so a formula using it can be summarised.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_roll_up_summary_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) requires that all users specify a contract is sent on each Opportunity prior to marking it as "Closed Won". UC wants to be able to report on how many Opportunities have sent Contracts compared to how many have a missing contract when the Opportunities closed. Which field type should an app builder configure to fulfill this requirement?
optionA: Text
optionC: Picklist
explanation:
A checkbox is the right type for a yes-or-no fact such as "contract sent", and it reports cleanly: a report grouped or filtered on the checkbox shows how many closed opportunities have the box checked against how many do not. A validation rule can then require the box to be checked before the stage becomes Closed Won.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Text) — free text such as "yes", "Y" or "sent" cannot be counted reliably.
Option B (Text Area) — the same problem, with more room for inconsistency.
Option C (Picklist) — workable but more than the requirement needs; a two-state fact is what checkboxes exist for, and a picklist adds blank as a third state to filter around.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.custom_field_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_validation_rules_tips.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers wants to create a report to show job applications with or without resumes. What considerations should the app builder be aware of when creating the custom report type?
optionA: An app builder is unable to create custom report types for objects they do not have permissions for.
optionB: Once the report type has been deployed it is unable to be deleted.
optionC: A primary object selection is locked once the custom report type has been saved.
optionD: When a custom or external object is deleted the report type and reports remain but cause an error when the report is run.
explanation:
Once saved, a custom report type's primary object is fixed: "After you save the report type, you can't change the primary object." Choose Job Application as the primary object and add Resume as a related object with "'A' records may or may not have related 'B' records" to get the with-or-without report.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Can't create report types for objects without permissions) — creating report types needs the Manage Custom Report Types permission, not object permissions on each object.
Option B (A deployed report type can't be deleted) — custom report types can be deleted; doing so deletes the reports built on them, which is the real consideration.
Option D (Deleting an object leaves the report type and reports in place) — deleting a custom object also deletes the custom report types and reports that reference it.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.reports_enhanced_defining_report_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A sales rep at AW Computing is unable to find what they are looking for while scrolling through their Chatter feed. How can a filter be utilized to show only posts from their key account and opportunity records?
optionA: Create a Chatter group.
optionC: Create a Chatter stream.
explanation:
A Chatter stream is a personal feed filtered to chosen records: "Chatter streams are custom feeds that you create by combining multiple related feeds into one feed ... create streams that combine feeds from people, groups, and records, like accounts, opportunities, cases, and more." A stream of the key account and opportunity records shows only their posts.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (A Chatter group) — a place for people to post together; it does not collect record feeds.
Option B (Chatter bookmarks) — save individual posts; they do not filter the feed.
Option D (A Chatter notification) — alerts about mentions and posts; not a filtered feed.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=experience.collab_chatter_streams_overview.htm&language=en_US&type=5
